112:   /** Conditions with `threshold_overrides` applied by field_path. */
113:   conditions: AlertRuleConditionRow[];
114:   /** Channel kinds requested by the winning scope chain. */
115:   requestedChannels: string[];
116:   actionMode: AlertActionMergeMode;
117:   recipientOverrides: Record<string, unknown> | null;
118:   escalationPolicyId: string | null;
119: 
120:   trace: RuleResolutionTraceEntry[];
121: }
122: 
123: /**
124:  * Whether a binding's scope tuple is a prefix match of the evaluation context.
125:  *
126:  * Organization always matches. Deeper scopes match only when the context specifies the
127:  * same value — a binding for `environment='production'` does not apply to an evaluation
128:  * with no environment, and never applies to a different environment.
129:  */
130: export function bindingMatchesScope(
131:   binding: AlertRuleBindingRow,
132:   scope: EvaluationScope,
133: ): boolean {
134:   if (binding.organization_id !== scope.organizationId) return false;
135:   if (binding.project_id !== null && binding.project_id !== (scope.projectId ?? null)) return false;
136:   if (binding.environment !== null && binding.environment !== (scope.environment ?? null)) return false;
137:   if (binding.service !== null && binding.service !== (scope.service ?? null)) return false;
138:   if (binding.endpoint !== null && binding.endpoint !== (scope.endpoint ?? null)) return false;
139:   return true;
140: }
141: 
142: /**
143:  * Deterministic ordering for the fold: shallowest first so deeper scopes overwrite.
144:  *
145:  * Equal depth is possible (e.g. two `service` bindings on the same project cannot both
146:  * match, but a `service` and an `endpoint` binding can tie after filtering). ADR-0004 §5
147:  * fixes the tie-break so resolution never depends on row order from the database.
148:  */
149: export function compareBindings(a: AlertRuleBindingRow, b: AlertRuleBindingRow): number {
150:   if (a.scope_level !== b.scope_level) return a.scope_level - b.scope_level;
151:   if (a.priority !== b.priority) return b.priority - a.priority;
152:   const at = a.created_at instanceof Date ? a.created_at.getTime() : new Date(a.created_at).getTime();
153:   const bt = b.created_at instanceof Date ? b.created_at.getTime() : new Date(b.created_at).getTime();
154:   if (at !== bt) return at - bt;
155:   return a.id.localeCompare(b.id);
156: }
157: 
158: function applyThresholdOverrides(
159:   conditions: AlertRuleConditionRow[],
160:   overrides: Record<string, unknown>,
161: ): AlertRuleConditionRow[] {
162:   const keys = Object.keys(overrides);
163:   if (keys.length === 0) return conditions;
164:   return conditions.map((condition) =>
165:     Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(overrides, condition.field_path)
166:       ? { ...condition, threshold_value: overrides[condition.field_path] }
167:       : condition,
168:   );
169: }
170: 
171: /**
172:  * Resolve exactly one effective rule for an evaluation scope.
173:  *
174:  * @param rule       the rule definition (organization-owned)
175:  * @param conditions the rule's conditions, in order
176:  * @param bindings    every binding for this rule; non-matching and soft-deleted rows are
177:  *                    filtered here so callers may pass the raw query result
178:  * @param scope      the evaluation context
179:  */
180: export function resolveEffectiveRule(
181:   rule: AlertRuleRow,
182:   conditions: AlertRuleConditionRow[],
183:   bindings: AlertRuleBindingRow[],
184:   scope: EvaluationScope,
185: ): EffectiveRule {
186:   const matching = bindings
187:     .filter((binding) => binding.deleted_at === null && bindingMatchesScope(binding, scope))
188:     .sort(compareBindings);
189:   const requiresProjectSubscription = Boolean(scope.projectId)
190:     && matching.some((binding) => binding.scope_type === 'organization')
191:     && !matching.some((binding) => binding.scope_level > SCOPE_LEVEL.organization);
192: 
193:   // Start from the rule's own values. A rule with no bindings resolves to exactly the
194:   // behaviour it has today — this is what makes the P12 backfill behaviour-identical.
195:   const effective: EffectiveRule = {
196:     ruleId: rule.id,
197:     organizationId: rule.organization_id,
198:     bindingId: null,
199:     resolvedScopeType: 'organization',
200:     resolvedScopeLevel: 0,
201:     enabled: rule.enabled,
202:     severity: rule.severity,
203:     cooldownSeconds: rule.cooldown_seconds,
204:     deduplicationWindowSeconds: rule.deduplication_window_seconds,
205:     evaluationIntervalSeconds: rule.evaluation_interval_seconds,
206:     autoResolveAfterMinutes: rule.auto_resolve_after_minutes,
207:     consecutiveBreaches: toConsecutiveBreaches(rule),
208:     conditions,
209:     requestedChannels: [],
210:     actionMode: 'inherit',
211:     recipientOverrides: null,
212:     escalationPolicyId: null,
213:     trace: [{
214:       bindingId: null,
215:       scopeType: 'organization',
216:       scopeLevel: 0,
217:       mode: 'base',
218:       applied: ['rule defaults'],
219:       note: `rule "${rule.name}"`,
220:     }],
221:   };
222: 
223:   let thresholdOverrides: Record<string, unknown> = {};
224: 
225:   for (const binding of matching) {
226:     const applied: string[] = [];
227: 
228:     // Step 3: disable stops the rule here; a deeper override may re-enable it.
229:     if (binding.mode === 'disable') {
230:       effective.enabled = false;
231:       applied.push('enabled=false (disable)');
232:     } else if (binding.mode === 'override') {
233:       if (effective.enabled !== binding.enabled) applied.push(`enabled=${binding.enabled}`);
234:       effective.enabled = binding.enabled;
235:     }
236: 
237:     // Step 2: sparse scalar overrides — NULL never overwrites.
238:     if (binding.severity !== null) { effective.severity = binding.severity; applied.push('severity'); }
239:     if (binding.cooldown_seconds !== null) {
240:       effective.cooldownSeconds = binding.cooldown_seconds; applied.push('cooldownSeconds');
241:     }
242:     if (binding.deduplication_window_seconds !== null) {
243:       effective.deduplicationWindowSeconds = binding.deduplication_window_seconds;
244:       applied.push('deduplicationWindowSeconds');
245:     }
246:     if (binding.evaluation_interval_seconds !== null) {
247:       effective.evaluationIntervalSeconds = binding.evaluation_interval_seconds;
248:       applied.push('evaluationIntervalSeconds');
249:     }
250:     if (binding.auto_resolve_after_minutes !== null) {
251:       effective.autoResolveAfterMinutes = binding.auto_resolve_after_minutes;
252:       applied.push('autoResolveAfterMinutes');
253:     }
254:     if (binding.consecutive_breaches !== null) {
255:       effective.consecutiveBreaches = binding.consecutive_breaches;
256:       applied.push('consecutiveBreaches');
257:     }
258: 
259:     // Threshold overrides accumulate per field_path, deepest scope winning each key.
260:     const overrideKeys = Object.keys(binding.threshold_overrides ?? {});
261:     if (overrideKeys.length > 0) {
262:       thresholdOverrides = { ...thresholdOverrides, ...binding.threshold_overrides };
263:       applied.push(`thresholds[${overrideKeys.join(',')}]`);
264:     }
265: 
266:     // Step 4: action/channel merge semantics.
267:     if (binding.action_mode !== 'inherit') {
268:       effective.actionMode = binding.action_mode;
269:       applied.push(`actionMode=${binding.action_mode}`);
270:     }
271:     if (binding.requested_channels !== null) {
272:       effective.requestedChannels = binding.action_mode === 'merge'
273:         ? [...new Set([...effective.requestedChannels, ...binding.requested_channels])]
274:         : [...binding.requested_channels];
275:       applied.push('requestedChannels');
276:     }
277:     if (binding.recipient_overrides !== null) {
278:       effective.recipientOverrides = binding.action_mode === 'merge' && effective.recipientOverrides
279:         ? { ...effective.recipientOverrides, ...binding.recipient_overrides }
280:         : { ...binding.recipient_overrides };
281:       applied.push('recipientOverrides');
282:     }
283:     if (binding.escalation_policy_id !== null) {
284:       effective.escalationPolicyId = binding.escalation_policy_id;
285:       applied.push('escalationPolicyId');
286:     }
287: 
288:     // Step 6: the deepest contributing binding identifies the resolved scope.
289:     effective.bindingId = binding.id;
290:     effective.resolvedScopeType = binding.scope_type;
291:     effective.resolvedScopeLevel = binding.scope_level;
292: 
293:     effective.trace.push({
294:       bindingId: binding.id,
295:       scopeType: binding.scope_type,
296:       scopeLevel: binding.scope_level,
297:       mode: binding.mode,
298:       applied,
299:     });
300:   }
301: 
302:   if (requiresProjectSubscription) {
303:     effective.enabled = false;
304:     effective.bindingId = null;
305:     effective.resolvedScopeType = 'project';
306:     effective.resolvedScopeLevel = SCOPE_LEVEL.project;
307:     effective.trace.push({
308:       bindingId: null,
309:       scopeType: 'project',
310:       scopeLevel: SCOPE_LEVEL.project,
311:       mode: 'disable',
312:       applied: ['enabled=false (project not subscribed)'],
313:       note: 'organization rule requires a matching project subscription binding',
314:     });
315:   }
316: 
317:   effective.conditions = applyThresholdOverrides(conditions, thresholdOverrides);
318:   return effective;
319: }
320: 
321: /**
322:  * Consecutive-breach count carried on the rule today.
323:  *
324:  * Preserves the existing evaluator contract: `metadata.consecutiveBreachesRequired` first,
325:  * then `annotations.consecutiveBreaches`, else 1.
326:  */
327: function toConsecutiveBreaches(rule: AlertRuleRow): number {
328:   const fromMetadata = (rule.metadata ?? {})['consecutiveBreachesRequired'];
329:   const fromAnnotations = (rule.annotations ?? {})['consecutiveBreaches'];
330:   for (const candidate of [fromMetadata, fromAnnotations]) {
331:     const value = typeof candidate === 'number'
332:       ? candidate
333:       : typeof candidate === 'string' ? Number(candidate) : NaN;
334:     if (Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 1) return value;
335:   }
336:   return 1;
337: }
338: 
339: /**
340:  * True when two equal-depth bindings tied and the tie-break had to decide.
341:  * Surfaced so `alert_binding_conflicts_total` can be incremented by the caller.
342:  */
343: export function hasEqualDepthConflict(
344:   bindings: AlertRuleBindingRow[],
345:   scope: EvaluationScope,
346: ): boolean {
347:   const matching = bindings
348:     .filter((binding) => binding.deleted_at === null && bindingMatchesScope(binding, scope));
349:   const seen = new Set<number>();
350:   for (const binding of matching) {
351:     if (seen.has(binding.scope_level)) return true;
352:     seen.add(binding.scope_level);
353:   }
354:   return false;
355: }

3: import type { EffectiveRuleQuery } from '../config/bindings.types.js';

5: import type { AlertCandidate, EffectiveAlertPolicy, PolicyResolutionResult } from './types.js';
6: 
7: export interface AlertPolicyEngineDeps {
8:   bindings?: AlertRuleBindingsService;
9:   logger: FastifyBaseLogger;
10: }
11: 
12: export class AlertPolicyEngine {
13:   private readonly bindings: AlertRuleBindingsService;
14:   private readonly cache = new AlertPolicyCache();
15:   private readonly log: FastifyBaseLogger;
16: 
17:   constructor(deps: AlertPolicyEngineDeps) {
18:     this.bindings = deps.bindings ?? new AlertRuleBindingsService({ logger: deps.logger });
19:     this.log = deps.logger.child({ component: 'alert-policy-engine' });
20:   }
21: 
22:   async resolve(candidate: AlertCandidate, version = 1): Promise<PolicyResolutionResult> {
23:     const scope: EffectiveRuleQuery = {
24:       ...(candidate.projectId ? { projectId: candidate.projectId } : {}),
25:       ...(candidate.environment ? { environment: candidate.environment } : {}),
26:       ...(candidate.service ? { service: candidate.service } : {}),
27:       ...(candidate.endpoint ? { endpoint: candidate.endpoint } : {}),
28:     };
29:     const key = policyCacheKey(candidate.organizationId, candidate.ruleId, version, {
30:       projectId: candidate.projectId ?? null,
31:       environment: candidate.environment ?? null,
32:       service: candidate.service ?? null,
33:       endpoint: candidate.endpoint ?? null,
34:     });
35:     const cached = this.cache.get(key);
36:     if (cached) return cached;
37: 
38:     const result = await this.bindings.resolveEffective(candidate.organizationId, candidate.ruleId, scope);
39:     const policy: EffectiveAlertPolicy = {
40:       policyId: `${candidate.organizationId}:${candidate.ruleId}:${version}`,
41:       version,
42:       organizationId: candidate.organizationId,
43:       ruleId: candidate.ruleId,
44:       scope: {
45:         organizationId: candidate.organizationId,
46:         projectId: candidate.projectId ?? null,
47:         environment: candidate.environment ?? null,
48:         service: candidate.service ?? null,
49:         endpoint: candidate.endpoint ?? null,
50:       },
51:       enabled: result.rule.enabled,
52:       severity: result.rule.severity,
53:       cooldownSeconds: result.rule.cooldownSeconds,
54:       deduplicationWindowSeconds: result.rule.deduplicationWindowSeconds,
55:       evaluationIntervalSeconds: result.rule.evaluationIntervalSeconds,
56:       autoResolveAfterMinutes: result.rule.autoResolveAfterMinutes,
57:       consecutiveBreaches: result.rule.consecutiveBreaches,
58:       conditions: result.rule.conditions,
59:       thresholds: result.thresholds,
60:       requestedChannels: [...result.rule.requestedChannels],
61:       recipientOverrides: result.rule.recipientOverrides
62:         ? { ...result.rule.recipientOverrides }
63:         : null,
64:       escalationPolicyId: result.rule.escalationPolicyId,
65:       trace: result.rule.trace.map((entry) => ({ ...entry, applied: [...entry.applied] })),
66:     };
67:     const resolved = {
68:       policy,
69:       conflict: result.conflict,
70:       appliedBindingIds: [...result.appliedBindingIds],
71:     } satisfies PolicyResolutionResult;
72:     this.cache.set(key, resolved);
73:     return resolved;
74:   }
75: 
76:   async simulate(candidate: AlertCandidate, version = 1): Promise<PolicyResolutionResult> {
77:     const startedAt = Date.now();
78:     try {
79:       return await this.resolve(candidate, version);
80:     } finally {
81:       this.log.debug({ ruleId: candidate.ruleId, durationMs: Date.now() - startedAt }, 'Alert policy simulated');
82:     }
83:   }
84: 
85:   invalidateRule(ruleId: string): void {
86:     this.cache.deleteByRule(ruleId);
87:   }
88: 
89:   clearCache(): void {
90:     this.cache.clear();
91:   }
92: }

179: function toSeverity(value: string): LogDbSeverity {
180:   if (value === 'debug' || value === 'info' || value === 'warning' || value === 'error' || value === 'critical' || value === 'fatal') return value;
181:   return 'error';
182: }
183: 
184: function severityPriority(value: string): number {
185:   return { debug: 0, info: 10, warning: 30, error: 70, critical: 90, fatal: 100 }[value] ?? 70;
186: }

266: export class AlertRuntimeRepository {
267:   /**
268:    * @param db The LOG DB pool (logDB.getPrimaryPool()). There is no default:
269:    *   defaulting would re-create the exact ambiguity ADR-0006 removes.
270:    */
271:   constructor(private readonly db: Pool) {}
272: 
273:   /** The pool this repository is bound to. Exposed for boot verification only. */
274:   get connectionPool(): Pool {
275:     return this.db;
276:   }
277: 
278:   /**
279:    * Boot assertion (ADR-0006): the runtime pool must resolve `events_requests`
280:    * (telemetry is visible) and `alert_events_v2` (Log DB migrations applied).
281:    */
282:   async assertRuntimePool(logger: Logger): Promise<AlertingPoolTarget> {
283:     return assertAlertingPool(this.db, 'alerting_runtime', logger);
284:   }
285: 
286:   /**
287:    * Runtime transaction. Scoped to the Log DB only — it can never span the control
288:    * plane, which is what makes the ADR-0006 boundary structural rather than advisory.
289:    */
290:   async withTransaction<T>(fn: (client: PoolClient) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
291:     const client = await this.db.connect();
292:     try {
293:       await client.query('BEGIN');
294:       const result = await fn(client);
295:       await client.query('COMMIT');
296:       return result;
297:     } catch (err) {
298:       await client.query('ROLLBACK').catch(() => undefined);
299:       throw err;
300:     } finally {
301:       client.release();
302:     }
303:   }
304: 
305:   private exec(client?: PoolClient): Pool | PoolClient {
306:     return client ?? this.db;
307:   }
308: 
309:   // ── alert_events_v2 (append-only) ───────────────────────────────────────────
310: 
311:   /**
312:    * Append an alert event.
313:    *
314:    * Returns `null` when `uq_alert_events_v2_idem` rejects the row, i.e. this exact
315:    * candidate was already decided. Callers treat null as "already handled" — that
316:    * is the exactly-once mechanism, and it lives in the index, not in code.
317:    */
318:   async appendEvent(
319:     input: AppendAlertEventInput,
320:     client?: PoolClient,
321:   ): Promise<AlertEventV2Row | null> {
322:     const result = await this.exec(client).query<AlertEventV2Row>(
323:       `WITH reserved AS (
324:          INSERT INTO alert_runtime_idempotency_keys (namespace, organization_id, idempotency_key)
325:          VALUES ('alert_event', $1, $18)
326:          ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
327:          RETURNING organization_id, idempotency_key
328:        )
329:        INSERT INTO alert_events_v2 (
330:          organization_id, project_id, environment, service, endpoint,
331:          rule_id, binding_id, rule_revision, kind, severity, priority,
332:          fingerprint, dedup_key, correlation_key, group_key, source, engine,
333:          idempotency_key, observed_value, threshold_value,
334:          evidence, policy_snapshot, labels, annotations, occurred_at
335:        )
336:        SELECT $1, $2, $3, $4, $5,
337:               $6, $7, $8, $9::alert_event_kind, $10::logdb_severity, $11,
338:               $12, $13, $14, $15, $16, $17,
339:               $18, $19, $20,
340:               $21::jsonb, $22::jsonb, $23::jsonb, $24::jsonb, $25
341:          FROM reserved
342:        ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
343:        RETURNING *`,
344:       [
345:         input.organizationId,
346:         input.projectId ?? null,
347:         input.environment ?? null,
348:         input.service ?? null,
349:         input.endpoint ?? null,
350:         input.ruleId ?? null,
351:         input.bindingId ?? null,
352:         input.ruleRevision ?? null,
353:         input.kind,
354:         input.severity,
355:         input.priority ?? 0,
356:         input.fingerprint,
357:         input.dedupKey,
358:         input.correlationKey ?? null,
359:         input.groupKey ?? null,
360:         input.source,
361:         input.engine,
362:         input.idempotencyKey,
363:         input.observedValue ?? null,
364:         input.thresholdValue ?? null,
365:         json(input.evidence),
366:         json(input.policySnapshot),
367:         json(input.labels),
368:         json(input.annotations),
369:         input.occurredAt,
370:       ],
371:     );
372:     return result.rows[0] ?? null;
373:   }
374: 
375:   async findEventById(
376:     organizationId: string,
377:     id: string,
378:     client?: PoolClient,
379:   ): Promise<AlertEventV2Row | null> {
380:     const result = await this.exec(client).query<AlertEventV2Row>(
381:       `SELECT * FROM alert_events_v2 WHERE id = $1 AND organization_id = $2
382:        ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1`,
383:       [id, organizationId],
384:     );

388:   // ── alert_event_state (the ONE mutable projection) ──────────────────────────

390:   async getState(alertKey: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<AlertEventStateRow | null> {
391:     const result = await this.exec(client).query<AlertEventStateRow>(
392:       `SELECT * FROM alert_event_state WHERE alert_key = $1`,
393:       [alertKey],
394:     );
395:     return result.rows[0] ?? null;
396:   }
397: 
398:   /**
399:    * Lock the state row for the duration of the caller's transaction.
400:    *
401:    * ADR-0007 relies on this to serialize concurrent decisions for the same alert
402:    * key, so two workers evaluating the same rule in the same second cannot both
403:    * fire. Requires an explicit client: a lock outside a transaction is meaningless.
404:    */
405:   async lockState(client: PoolClient, alertKey: string): Promise<AlertEventStateRow | null> {
406:     const result = await client.query<AlertEventStateRow>(
407:       `SELECT * FROM alert_event_state WHERE alert_key = $1 FOR UPDATE`,
408:       [alertKey],
409:     );
410:     return result.rows[0] ?? null;
411:   }
412: 
413:   /**
414:    * Insert or advance the alert state projection.
415:    *
416:    * `first_seen_at` is preserved on update; `last_seen_at` moves forward monotonically
417:    * so an out-of-order redelivery cannot rewind it. `duplicate_count` is untouched
418:    * here — {@link incrementDuplicate} owns it, keeping the two concerns separate.
419:    */
420:   async upsertState(input: UpsertAlertStateInput, client?: PoolClient): Promise<AlertEventStateRow> {
421:     const result = await this.exec(client).query<AlertEventStateRow>(
422:       `INSERT INTO alert_event_state (
423:          alert_key, organization_id, project_id, latest_event_id, state, severity,
424:          first_seen_at, last_seen_at, last_notified_at, auto_resolve_at,
425:          escalation_policy_id, escalation_step_number, next_escalation_at, incident_id
426:        ) VALUES (
427:          $1, $2, $3, $4, $5::alert_state, $6::logdb_severity,
428:          $7, $7, $8, $9, $10, $11, $12, $13
429:        )
430:        ON CONFLICT (alert_key) DO UPDATE SET
431:          latest_event_id        = EXCLUDED.latest_event_id,
432:          state                  = EXCLUDED.state,
433:          severity               = EXCLUDED.severity,
434:          last_seen_at           = GREATEST(alert_event_state.last_seen_at, EXCLUDED.last_seen_at),
435:          last_notified_at       = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.last_notified_at, alert_event_state.last_notified_at),
436:          auto_resolve_at        = EXCLUDED.auto_resolve_at,
437:          escalation_policy_id   = EXCLUDED.escalation_policy_id,
438:          escalation_step_number = EXCLUDED.escalation_step_number,
439:          next_escalation_at     = EXCLUDED.next_escalation_at,
440:          incident_id            = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.incident_id, alert_event_state.incident_id)
441:        RETURNING *`,
442:       [
443:         input.alertKey,
444:         input.organizationId,
445:         input.projectId ?? null,
446:         input.latestEventId,
447:         input.state,
448:         input.severity,
449:         input.seenAt,
450:         input.notifiedAt ?? null,
451:         input.autoResolveAt ?? null,
452:         input.escalationPolicyId ?? null,
453:         input.escalationStepNumber ?? 0,
454:         input.nextEscalationAt ?? null,
455:         input.incidentId ?? null,
456:       ],
457:     );
458:     return result.rows[0]!;
459:   }

461:   /** Fold a duplicate into the existing alert. Never billed (ADR-0010). */
462:   async incrementDuplicate(
463:     alertKey: string,
464:     seenAt: Date,
465:     client?: PoolClient,
466:   ): Promise<AlertEventStateRow | null> {
467:     const result = await this.exec(client).query<AlertEventStateRow>(
468:       `UPDATE alert_event_state
469:           SET duplicate_count = duplicate_count + 1,
470:               last_seen_at = GREATEST(last_seen_at, $2)
471:         WHERE alert_key = $1
472:         RETURNING *`,
473:       [alertKey, seenAt],
474:     );
475:     return result.rows[0] ?? null;
476:   }

486:          $1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6,
487:          $7::alert_state, $8::alert_state, $9::jsonb, $10::jsonb
488:        )`,

504:   async listHistory(alertKey: string, limit = 200): Promise<Array<Record<string, unknown>>> {
505:     const result = await this.db.query(

507:               changes_summary, metadata, created_at

509:         WHERE alert_key = $1

517:   // ── alert_notification_jobs (append-only, unique idempotency key) ───────────
518: 
519:   /**
520:    * Bulk-insert notification jobs in ONE statement (no N+1).
521:    *
522:    * `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` against `uq_alert_notification_jobs_idem` is what
523:    * delivers the "zero duplicate notifications" success criterion: a retried
524:    * decision job cannot create a second job for the same
525:    * (alert, channel, recipient, escalation step, attempt epoch).
526:    *
527:    * Returns only the rows actually inserted, so the caller can publish exactly
528:    * those and count usage for exactly those.
529:    */
530:   async insertNotificationJobs(
531:     rows: NotificationJobInsert[],
532:     client?: PoolClient,
533:   ): Promise<NotificationJobRow[]> {
534:     if (rows.length === 0) return [];
535:     const result = await this.exec(client).query<NotificationJobRow>(
536:       `WITH input AS (
537:          SELECT t.*
538:            FROM UNNEST(
539:              $1::uuid[], $2::uuid[], $3::uuid[], $4::text[], $5::text[],
540:              $6::uuid[], $7::uuid[], $8::uuid[], $9::text[], $10::uuid[],
541:              $11::text[], $12::smallint[], $13::smallint[], $14::smallint[], $15::jsonb[],
542:              $16::text[], $17::boolean[], $18::timestamptz[]
543:            ) AS t(organization_id, project_id, alert_event_id, alert_key, channel_kind,
544:                   connector_id, route_id, recipient_user_id, recipient_ref, template_id,
545:                   severity, priority, escalation_step, attempt_epoch, payload,
546:                   idempotency_key, billable, notify_after)
547:        ), reserved AS (
548:          INSERT INTO alert_runtime_idempotency_keys (namespace, organization_id, idempotency_key)
549:          SELECT 'notification_job', organization_id, idempotency_key
550:            FROM input
551:          ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
552:          RETURNING organization_id, idempotency_key
553:        )
554:        INSERT INTO alert_notification_jobs (
555:          organization_id, project_id, alert_event_id, alert_key, channel_kind,
556:          connector_id, route_id, recipient_user_id, recipient_ref, template_id,
557:          severity, priority, escalation_step, attempt_epoch, payload,
558:          idempotency_key, billable, notify_after
559:        )
560:        SELECT t.organization_id, t.project_id, t.alert_event_id, t.alert_key,
561:               t.channel_kind::notification_channel_kind,
562:               t.connector_id, t.route_id, t.recipient_user_id, t.recipient_ref, t.template_id,
563:               t.severity::logdb_severity, t.priority, t.escalation_step, t.attempt_epoch,
564:               t.payload, t.idempotency_key, t.billable, t.notify_after
565:          FROM input t
566:          JOIN reserved r
567:            ON r.organization_id = t.organization_id
568:           AND r.idempotency_key = t.idempotency_key
569:        ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
570:        RETURNING id, created_at, idempotency_key, channel_kind, status`,
571:       [
572:         rows.map((r) => r.organizationId),

1: /**
2:  * Scheduled alert-rule evaluation engine (worker path ONLY — never HTTP).
3:  *
4:  * Driven by the pg-boss cron queue `alert.evaluate-rules` (see
5:  * alerting/queue.ts). Each tick:
6:  *   1. Selects enabled rules whose evaluation interval has elapsed
7:  *      (watermark: alert_rules.last_evaluated_at), bounded + oldest-first.
8:  *   2. Evaluates every condition of a rule against the observability event
9:  *      tables with a single bounded query per condition (see CONDITION SQL
10:  *      below). Unmappable conditions are skipped (debug log, fail-open).
11:  *   3. Combines condition outcomes with the shared grouping semantics of
12:  *      alerting/evaluator.ts (groups OR'd, ungrouped AND'd).
13:  *   4. Consecutive-breach counting in alert_rules.metadata->>'consecutiveBreaches'
14:  *      (required count from metadata.consecutiveBreachesRequired /
15:  *      annotations.consecutiveBreaches, default 1).
16:  *   5. Cooldown: an active alert_events row with the same fingerprint within
17:  *      cooldown_seconds suppresses re-firing.
18:  *   6. FIRE via EventsService.ingestEvent (the single ingestion entry point —
19:  *      fingerprint/dedup/silence/pending persist all stay in one place).
20:  *   7. RECOVERY: when a previously-breaching rule evaluates clear, any active
21:  *      event with the rule's fingerprint is resolved (resolution_reason
22:  *      'auto') so the alert auto-resolves.
23:  *   8. last_evaluated_at advances on success (incl. mapped-skip) but NOT on
24:  *      query error, so a failed rule is retried on the next tick.
25:  *
26:  * One bad rule never breaks the tick: every rule runs inside its own
27:  * try/catch and the tick processes rules with bounded concurrency.
28:  */
29: import type { FastifyBaseLogger } from 'fastify';
30: import type { Pool } from 'pg';
31: import { pool } from '../../../config/database.js';
32: import { AlertingRepository } from '../repository.js';
33: import { EventsService } from '../events/events.service.js';
34: import { evaluateRule, type EvaluableCondition } from '../evaluator.js';
35: import { seedDefaultPresetsForOrg } from './presets.js';
36: import { ProjectThresholdWorker } from '../../projects/alerts/thresholds/threshold.worker.js';
37: import type { AlertRuleConditionRow, AlertRuleRow } from '../types.js';
38: 
39: const EVAL_SOURCE = 'rule-evaluator';
40: const RULE_BATCH_LIMIT = 500;
41: const RULE_CONCURRENCY = 10;
42: /** Hard cap for the log-pattern scan (LIMIT guard) so a noisy window stays cheap. */
43: const LOG_SCAN_LIMIT = 10_000;
44: 
45: export interface EvaluatorTickSummary {
46:   rulesDue: number;
47:   evaluated: number;
48:   fired: number;
49:   recovered: number;
50:   cooldownSkipped: number;
51:   failed: number;
52:   orgsSeeded: number;
53: }
54: 
55: interface ConditionOutcome {
56:   condition: AlertRuleConditionRow;
57:   /** Whether the condition could be mapped + queried. */
58:   evaluated: boolean;
59:   /** The computed scalar (null when the query yielded no data). */
60:   actual: unknown;
61:   /** Operator/threshold actually compared (log matches are normalized). */
62:   operator: AlertRuleConditionRow['operator'];
63:   threshold: unknown;
64: }
65: 
66: export class AlertRuleEvaluator {
67:   private readonly repo = new AlertingRepository();
68:   private readonly eventsService: EventsService;
69:   private readonly projectThresholds: ProjectThresholdWorker;
70:   private readonly log: FastifyBaseLogger;
71:   /**
72:    * Pool that owns TELEMETRY (`events_*`). ADR-0006 / DEV-002: ingestion persists telemetry
73:    * through the Log DB pool, so the evaluator must read it through the same pool. Defaults to
74:    * the control-plane pool so single-database deployments behave exactly as before.
75:    *
76:    * NOTE: `ai_usage_logs`, `alert_rules` and `alert_events` are NOT telemetry — they stay on
77:    * the control-plane pool. Only `events_*` reads are routed here.
78:    */
79:   private readonly telemetry: Pool;
80:   /** When true, conditions are evaluated and logged but no alert is fired or auto-resolved. */
81:   private readonly dryRun: boolean;
82: 
83:   /**
84:    * @param telemetryPool pool owning `events_*`; defaults to the control-plane pool
85:    * @param dryRun explicit override. When omitted it defaults to "dry-run if the telemetry pool
86:    *   is a different pool", so single-database deployments keep firing exactly as before.
87:    *   The environment-driven value is resolved by the worker registration (see
88:    *   `resolveEvaluatorDryRun`) and passed in, keeping this class free of env coupling.
89:    */
90:   constructor(logger: FastifyBaseLogger, telemetryPool: Pool = pool, dryRun?: boolean) {
91:     this.log = logger.child({ component: 'alert-rule-evaluator' });
92:     this.eventsService = new EventsService({ repository: this.repo, logger });
93:     this.telemetry = telemetryPool;
94: 
95:     const poolsDiffer = this.telemetry !== pool;
96:     this.dryRun = dryRun ?? poolsDiffer;
97:     this.projectThresholds = new ProjectThresholdWorker(logger, telemetryPool, this.dryRun);
98: 
99:     this.log.info(
100:       {
101:         telemetryPoolIsSeparate: poolsDiffer,
102:         dryRun: this.dryRun,
103:         dryRunSource: dryRun === undefined ? 'auto' : 'explicit',
104:       },
105:       this.dryRun
106:         ? 'Alert rule evaluator running in DRY-RUN: conditions are evaluated but no alert will '
107:           + 'fire or auto-resolve (DEV-002). Set ALERTING_EVAL_DRY_RUN=false after parity validation.'
108:         : 'Alert rule evaluator will fire alerts',
109:     );
110:   }
111: 
112:   /** One evaluator tick: alert rules, project thresholds, and preset seeding. */
113:   async runTick(limit: number = RULE_BATCH_LIMIT): Promise<EvaluatorTickSummary> {
114:     const summary: EvaluatorTickSummary = {
115:       rulesDue: 0, evaluated: 0, fired: 0, recovered: 0, cooldownSkipped: 0, failed: 0, orgsSeeded: 0,
116:     };
117: 
118:     const [due, thresholdSummary] = await Promise.all([
119:       this.findDueRules(limit),
120:       this.projectThresholds.runTick(limit),
121:     ]);
122:     summary.rulesDue = due.length + thresholdSummary.due;
123:     summary.evaluated += thresholdSummary.evaluated;
124:     summary.fired += thresholdSummary.fired;
125:     summary.recovered += thresholdSummary.recovered;
126:     summary.failed += thresholdSummary.failed;
127: 
128:     await mapBounded(due, RULE_CONCURRENCY, async (rule) => {
129:       try {
130:         const outcome = await this.evaluateOneRule(rule);
131:         summary.evaluated += 1;
132:         if (outcome === 'fired') summary.fired += 1;
133:         else if (outcome === 'recovered') summary.recovered += 1;
134:         else if (outcome === 'cooldown') summary.cooldownSkipped += 1;
135:       } catch (err) {
136:         // Query/transient error: last_evaluated_at is intentionally NOT
137:         // advanced so the rule is retried on the next tick.
138:         summary.failed += 1;
139:         this.log.error({ err, ruleId: rule.id, orgId: rule.organization_id }, 'Rule evaluation failed');
140:       }
141:     });
142: 
143:     summary.orgsSeeded = await this.seedPresetsForActiveOrgs();
144:     if (summary.evaluated > 0 || summary.fired > 0 || summary.orgsSeeded > 0 || summary.failed > 0) {
145:       this.log.info({ ...summary }, 'Rule and project-threshold evaluation tick finished');
146:     }
147:     return summary;
148:   }
149: 
150:   /** Enabled rules due for evaluation, oldest watermark first, bounded. */
151:   private async findDueRules(limit: number): Promise<AlertRuleRow[]> {
152:     const r = await pool.query<AlertRuleRow>(
153:       `SELECT * FROM alert_rules
154:        WHERE enabled AND deleted_at IS NULL
155:          AND (last_evaluated_at IS NULL
156:               OR last_evaluated_at + evaluation_interval_seconds * interval '1 second' <= now())
157:        ORDER BY last_evaluated_at ASC NULLS FIRST
158:        LIMIT $1`,
159:       [limit],
160:     );
161:     return r.rows;
162:   }
163: 
164:   /**
165:    * Evaluate one rule end-to-end. Returns the outcome for tick metrics.
166:    * Throws on query error (the caller catches and leaves the watermark).
167:    */
168:   private async evaluateOneRule(rule: AlertRuleRow): Promise<'fired' | 'breaching' | 'cooldown' | 'recovered' | 'clear' | 'no_conditions'> {
169:     const [conditions] = await Promise.all([this.repo.getRuleConditions(rule.id)]);
170:     if (conditions.length === 0) {
171:       await this.markEvaluated(rule.id, 0);
172:       return 'no_conditions';
173:     }
174: 
175:     // 1–2. Evaluate each condition (bounded single-round-trip queries).
176:     const outcomes: ConditionOutcome[] = [];
177:     for (const condition of conditions) {
178:       outcomes.push(await this.evaluateCondition(rule, condition));
179:     }
180:     const evaluated = outcomes.filter((o) => o.evaluated);
181:     if (evaluated.length === 0) {
182:       // Every condition was unmappable — mapped-skip still advances the watermark.
183:       await this.markEvaluated(rule.id, 0);
184:       return 'no_conditions';
185:     }
186: 
187:     // Combine via the shared grouping semantics (groups OR, ungrouped AND).
188:     const payload: Record<string, unknown> = {};
189:     const evaluable: EvaluableCondition[] = [];
190:     for (const o of evaluated) {
191:       setPath(payload, o.condition.field_path, o.actual);
192:       evaluable.push({
193:         id: o.condition.id,
194:         conditionGroupId: o.condition.condition_group_id,
195:         fieldPath: o.condition.field_path,
196:         operator: o.operator,
197:         thresholdValue: o.threshold,
198:         isRequired: o.condition.is_required,
199:       });
200:     }
201:     const matched = evaluateRule(payload, evaluable).matched;
202: 
203:     // 3. Consecutive-breach accounting.
204:     const metadata = (rule.metadata ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
205:     const required = toPositiveInt(
206:       metadata.consecutiveBreachesRequired ?? (rule.annotations as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.consecutiveBreaches,
207:       1,
208:     );
209:     const previous = toNonNegativeInt(metadata.consecutiveBreaches, 0);
210: 
211:     if (matched) {
212:       const current = previous + 1;
213:       await this.markEvaluated(rule.id, current);
214:       if (current < required) return 'breaching';
215: 
216:       // 4. Cooldown: an active event with the same fingerprint inside the
217:       //    cooldown window suppresses re-firing.
218:       const fingerprint = this.fingerprintFor(rule);
219:       const existing = await this.repo.findActiveEventByFingerprint(
220:         rule.organization_id, fingerprint, rule.cooldown_seconds, rule.project_id,
221:       );
222:       if (existing) return 'cooldown';
223: 
224:       // 5. FIRE through the single ingestion entry point.
225:       await this.fire(rule, fingerprint, outcomes, current);
226:       return 'fired';
227:     }
228: 
229:     // Clear: reset the breach counter + advance the watermark.
230:     await this.markEvaluated(rule.id, 0);
231: 
232:     // 6. RECOVERY: resolve previously-firing events for this rule fingerprint.
233:     if (previous > 0) {
234:       const resolved = await this.recover(rule);
235:       return resolved > 0 ? 'recovered' : 'clear';
236:     }
237:     return 'clear';
238:   }
239: 
240:   /** Advance the watermark + persist the consecutive-breach counter atomically. */
241:   private async markEvaluated(ruleId: string, consecutiveBreaches: number): Promise<void> {
242:     await pool.query(
243:       `UPDATE alert_rules
244:        SET last_evaluated_at = now(),
245:            metadata = jsonb_set(COALESCE(metadata, '{}'::jsonb), '{consecutiveBreaches}', to_jsonb($2::int), true)
246:        WHERE id = $1`,
247:       [ruleId, consecutiveBreaches],
248:     );
249:   }
250: 
251:   /** Dedup/cooldown fingerprint: rule.id + ':' + (project_id ?? 'org') + ':' + source. */
252:   private fingerprintFor(rule: AlertRuleRow): string {
253:     return `${rule.id}:${rule.project_id ?? 'org'}:${EVAL_SOURCE}`;
254:   }
255: 
256:   /** Fire the rule via EventsService.ingestEvent (dedup/silence/pending persist). */
257:   private async fire(
258:     rule: AlertRuleRow,
259:     fingerprint: string,
260:     outcomes: ConditionOutcome[],
261:     consecutiveBreaches: number,
262:   ): Promise<void> {
263:     const lookbackMinutes = Math.max(1, ...outcomes.map((o) => o.condition.lookback_minutes ?? 1));
264:     const conditionSummaries = outcomes.map((o) => ({
265:       fieldPath: o.condition.field_path,
266:       operator: o.operator,
267:       threshold: o.threshold,
268:       actual: o.actual,
269:       evaluated: o.evaluated,
270:     }));
271:     const breaching = outcomes.find((o) => o.evaluated);
272: 
273:     // DEV-002 dry-run: the breach is real and fully evaluated, but no alert event is created,
274:     // so no notification can be delivered. This is what prevents an alert storm when the
275:     // evaluator starts seeing telemetry it could not previously read.
276:     if (this.dryRun) {
277:       this.log.warn(
278:         {
279:           ruleId: rule.id,
280:           orgId: rule.organization_id,
281:           projectId: rule.project_id,
282:           fingerprint,
283:           consecutiveBreaches,
284:           actual: breaching?.actual ?? null,
285:           threshold: breaching?.threshold ?? null,
286:           lookbackMinutes,
287:         },
288:         'DRY-RUN: alert rule would have fired (no alert event created)',
289:       );
290:       return;
291:     }
292: 
293:     await this.eventsService.ingestEvent(rule.organization_id, {

295:       projectId: rule.project_id ?? undefined,
296:       severity: rule.severity,
297:       source: EVAL_SOURCE,
298:       fingerprint,

301:         message: `${rule.name} breached its threshold (value ${formatActual(breaching?.actual)}, window ${lookbackMinutes}m)`,

303:         threshold: breaching?.threshold ?? null,
304:         window: { lookbackMinutes },

313:         source: EVAL_SOURCE,
314:       },
315:       annotations: { consecutiveBreaches, evaluatedAt: new Date().toISOString() },

320:     );
321:   }

323:   /** Resolve all active events carrying the rule fingerprint (auto-recovery). */
324:   private async recover(rule: AlertRuleRow): Promise<number> {
325:     // DEV-002 dry-run: auto-resolve is also a state mutation, so it is suppressed too.
326:     // Resolving alerts that a dry-run evaluator never fired would corrupt real alert state.
327:     if (this.dryRun) return 0;
328: 
329:     // alert_events is control-plane owned in this increment (legacy runtime), so this
330:     // deliberately stays on the primary pool — only `events_*` moved to the telemetry pool.
331:     const active = await pool.query<{ id: string }>(
332:       `SELECT id FROM alert_events
333:        WHERE organization_id = $1 AND fingerprint = $2
334:          AND status IN ('firing', 'acknowledged', 'pending', 'processing')
335:          AND ($3::uuid IS NULL OR project_id = $3)
336:        ORDER BY started_at DESC
337:        LIMIT 50`,
338:       [rule.organization_id, this.fingerprintFor(rule), rule.project_id],
339:     );
340:     for (const row of active.rows) {
341:       await this.repo.resolveEvent(rule.organization_id, row.id, null, 'auto', true);

343:         eventId: row.id, organizationId: rule.organization_id,
344:         action: 'auto_resolved', actorId: null, actorType: 'worker',
345:         metadata: { reason: 'condition_cleared', ruleId: rule.id },
346:       });
347:     }
348:     if (active.rows.length > 0) {
349:       this.log.info(
350:         { ruleId: rule.id, orgId: rule.organization_id, resolved: active.rows.length },
351:         'Alert rule recovered',
352:       );
353:     }
354:     return active.rows.length;
355:   }

357:   // ── Condition → SQL mapping ─────────────────────────────────────────────

359:   // Every query shares the same scope fragment:
360:   //   organization_id = $2
361:   //   AND timestamp >= now() - (GREATEST($1::int, 1) || ' minutes')::interval
362:   //   AND ($3::uuid IS NULL OR project_id = $3)
363:   // where $1 = lookbackMinutes, $2 = rule.organization_id, $3 = rule.project_id.
364:   //
365:   // kinds:
366:   //   error_count        events_errors count
367:   //   error_rate         100 * errors / NULLIF(requests, 0)  (CTE, both tables)
368:   //   request_count      events_requests count
369:   //   latency_avg        avg(latency_ms)
370:   //   latency_p95/p99    percentile_cont(0.95/0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms)
371:   //   5xx_rate           100 * count(status_code >= 500) / count(*)
372:   //   degraded_rate      100 * count(status_code >= 500 OR latency_ms >= 10000) / count(*)
373:   //   cron_failures      events_cron_checkins count(status = 'error')
374:   //   log_error_count    events_logs count(level = 'error')
375:   //   log_matches        events_logs count(message ILIKE/~ pattern) w/ LIMIT guard
376:   //   inactivity_minutes minutes since last events_requests row (1e9 when none)
377:   //   ai_failed_requests ai_usage_logs count(status != success)
378:   //   ai_duration_p95    percentile_cont(0.95) over ai_usage_logs.duration_ms
379:   //   ai_credits_used    sum(ai_usage_logs.credits_used)
380:   //   ai_cost_usd        sum(ai_usage_logs.estimated_cost_usd)
381:   //   ai_tokens_used     sum(ai_usage_logs.total_tokens)
382:   //   metric:<name>      aggregateFunction over events_metrics.value

384:   private async evaluateCondition(rule: AlertRuleRow, condition: AlertRuleConditionRow): Promise<ConditionOutcome> {
385:     const base: ConditionOutcome = {
386:       condition, evaluated: false, actual: null,
387:       operator: condition.operator, threshold: condition.threshold_value,
388:     };
389:     const lookback = Math.max(1, condition.lookback_minutes ?? 5);
390:     const kind = mapFieldPathToKind(condition.field_path, condition.aggregate_function);
391:     if (!kind) {
392:       this.log.debug(
393:         { ruleId: rule.id, conditionId: condition.id, fieldPath: condition.field_path },
394:         'Condition fieldPath not mappable to an event query — skipping (fail-open)',
395:       );
396:       return base;
397:     }
398: 
399:     const params: unknown[] = [lookback, rule.organization_id, rule.project_id];
400:     let sql: string;
401:     // Log-pattern conditions compare count >= 1; the pattern is the threshold value.
402:     let operator: ConditionOutcome['operator'] = condition.operator;
403:     let threshold: unknown = condition.threshold_value;
404: 
405:     const scope = `organization_id = $2
406:        AND occurred_at >= now() - (GREATEST($1::int, 1) || ' minutes')::interval
407:        AND ($3::uuid IS NULL OR project_id = $3)`;
408: 
409:     switch (kind.name) {
410:       case 'error_count':
411:         sql = `SELECT count(*)::float8 AS value FROM events_errors WHERE ${scope}`;
412:         break;
413:       case 'error_rate':
414:         sql = `WITH e AS (SELECT count(*)::float8 AS n FROM events_errors WHERE ${scope}),
415:                     r AS (SELECT count(*)::float8 AS n FROM events_requests WHERE ${scope})
416:                SELECT CASE WHEN r.n > 0 THEN 100.0 * e.n / r.n ELSE NULL END AS value FROM e, r`;
417:         break;
418:       case 'request_count':
419:         sql = `SELECT count(*)::float8 AS value FROM events_requests WHERE ${scope}`;
420:         break;
421:       case 'latency_avg':
422:         sql = `SELECT avg(latency_ms)::float8 AS value FROM events_requests WHERE ${scope}`;
423:         break;
424:       case 'latency_p95':
425:         sql = `SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms)::float8 AS value FROM events_requests WHERE ${scope}`;
426:         break;
427:       case 'latency_p99':
428:         sql = `SELECT percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms)::float8 AS value FROM events_requests WHERE ${scope}`;
429:         break;
430:       case '5xx_rate':
431:         sql = `SELECT CASE WHEN count(*) > 0
432:                       THEN 100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status_code >= 500) / count(*)
433:                       ELSE NULL END AS value
434:                FROM events_requests WHERE ${scope}`;
435:         break;
436:       case 'degraded_rate':
437:         sql = `SELECT CASE WHEN count(*) > 0
438:                       THEN 100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status_code >= 500 OR latency_ms >= 10000) / count(*)
439:                       ELSE NULL END AS value
440:                FROM events_requests WHERE ${scope}`;
441:         break;
442:       case 'cron_failures':
443:         sql = `SELECT count(*)::float8 AS value FROM events_cron_checkins WHERE ${scope} AND status = 'error'`;
444:         break;
445:       case 'log_error_count':
446:         sql = `SELECT count(*)::float8 AS value FROM events_logs WHERE ${scope} AND level = 'error'`;
447:         break;
448:       case 'log_matches': {
449:         const pattern = typeof condition.threshold_value === 'string' ? condition.threshold_value : null;
450:         if (!pattern) {
451:           this.log.debug({ ruleId: rule.id, conditionId: condition.id }, 'log_matches condition has no string pattern — skipping');

The core V2 resolver is already pure, deterministic, scoped through endpoint level, and cache-aware; the key defect is that runtime evaluation and notification creation bypass its downstream routing responsibilities. I’m checking configuration APIs, threshold workers, worker registration, and schema constraints now so the plan can specify exact file-level changes and safe deprecation gates.

 * This class owns ONLY mutable configuration and identity:

 *   alert_escalation_policies, alert_escalation_steps, alert_templates,
 *   alert_routing_rules.

 * It composes the existing per-domain repositories rather than duplicating their
 * SQL, so Increment 1 changes no queries and therefore no behaviour. What changes
 * is that the pool is now explicit and single-valued: constructing this class with
 * the Log DB pool is a programming error, and `assertConfigPool` proves at boot

export class AlertConfigRepository {
  private readonly db: Pool;
  private readonly rules: RulesRepository;
  private readonly silences: SilencesRepository;
  private readonly policies: PoliciesRepository;
  private readonly templates: TemplatesRepository;
  private readonly routing: RoutingRepository;

  /**
   * @param db The PRIMARY control-plane pool. Defaults to config/database.ts so
   *   existing construction sites keep working unchanged.
   */
  constructor(db: Pool = primaryPool) {
    this.db = db;
    this.rules = new RulesRepository(db);
    this.silences = new SilencesRepository(db);
    this.policies = new PoliciesRepository(db);
    this.templates = new TemplatesRepository(db);
    this.routing = new RoutingRepository(db);

  /** The pool this repository is bound to. Exposed for boot verification only. */
  get connectionPool(): Pool {

  async assertConfigPool(logger: Logger): Promise<AlertingPoolTarget> {
    return assertAlertingPool(this.db, 'alerting_config', logger);
  }

  /** Config-scoped transaction. Never spans the Log DB (ADR-0006). */
  async withTransaction<T>(fn: (client: PoolClient) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
    const client = await this.db.connect();
    try {
      await client.query('BEGIN');
      const result = await fn(client);
      await client.query('COMMIT');
      return result;
    } catch (err) {
      await client.query('ROLLBACK').catch(() => undefined);
      throw err;
    } finally {
      client.release();
    }
  }
