124	function deduplicateRecipients(
125	  recipients: Array<{ userId: string; email: string }>,
126	): Array<{ userId: string; email: string }> {
127	  const seen = new Set<string>();
128	  return recipients.filter((recipient) => {
129	    const email = recipient.email.trim().toLowerCase();
130	    if (!email || seen.has(email)) return false;
131	    seen.add(email);
132	    return true;
133	  }).map((recipient) => ({ ...recipient, email: recipient.email.trim().toLowerCase() }));
134	}

66:  * LogDatabaseManager — enterprise-grade dual-pool manager for the dedicated log

68:  *
69:  * Design goals:
70:  * - **Never time out ingestion.** Writes run with a separate, by-default
71:  *   unbounded statement timeout so large batch inserts and background
72:  *   maintenance are never aborted. Reads stay bounded to contain runaway
73:  *   analytical queries. Timeouts are applied with `SET LOCAL` inside a
74:  *   transaction so they can never leak onto a pooled connection.
75:  * - **Dual pool.** Primary handles writes/DDL; replica absorbs read traffic and
76:  *   transparently falls back to primary when absent or unhealthy.
77:  * - **TimescaleDB.** On connect (when enabled) the event tables are promoted to
78:  *   hypertables with compression + retention policies. Every step is idempotent
79:  *   and non-fatal — failure degrades cleanly to plain PostgreSQL.
80:  * - **High-throughput batch ingest** via set-based `UNNEST` inserts.
81:  * - **Resilience.** Exponential backoff with jitter, fast-fail on
82:  *   non-retryable errors, TCP keepalive, and a load-balancer health probe.

84: class LogDatabaseManager {

97:     if (env.LOG_DB_REPLICA && env.LOG_DB_REPLICA !== env.LOG_DB_PRIMARY) {
98:       dbLogger.info('Replica pool configured — read queries will be routed to the replica');

107:    * on the pool. A hard global timeout silently kills legitimate long-running
108:    * ingestion batches, COPY, and TimescaleDB maintenance. Instead, timeouts are
109:    * applied per-statement via `SET LOCAL`, scoped to the read path only.
110:    */

117:       idleTimeoutMillis: env.LOG_DB_IDLE_TIMEOUT,

119:       application_name: `${appName}_${env.NODE_ENV}`,
120:       keepAlive: env.LOG_DB_KEEPALIVE_MS > 0,
121:       keepAliveInitialDelayMillis: env.LOG_DB_KEEPALIVE_MS,
122:       allowExitOnIdle: false,

126:     const pool = new Pool(config);
127:     this.setupPoolMonitoring(pool, appName);
128:     return pool;

131:   private resolveSslConfig(connectionString: string, appName: string): PoolConfig['ssl'] {
132:     if (env.LOG_DB_SSL_ENABLED !== undefined) {
133:       return env.LOG_DB_SSL_ENABLED
134:         ? { rejectUnauthorized: env.LOG_DB_SSL_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED }
135:         : false;
136:     }
137: 
138:     try {
139:       const url = new URL(connectionString);
140:       const sslMode = url.searchParams.get('sslmode')?.toLowerCase();
141:       if (sslMode === 'disable') return false;
142:       if (
143:         sslMode === 'require' ||
144:         sslMode === 'verify-ca' ||
145:         sslMode === 'verify-full' ||
146:         sslMode === 'prefer' ||
147:         sslMode === 'allow'
148:       ) {
149:         return { rejectUnauthorized: env.LOG_DB_SSL_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED };
150:       }
151:     } catch {
152:       dbLogger.warn({ appName }, 'Invalid log DB connection string while inferring SSL; defaulting to SSL disabled');
153:     }
154: 
155:     return false;
156:   }
157: 
158:   private setupPoolMonitoring(pool: Pool, name: string): void {
159:     pool.on('connect', () => {
160:       dbLogger.debug({ pool: name }, 'New connection added to pool');
161:     });
162: 
163:     // Idle server-side disconnects are expected with managed providers; only
164:     // surface genuinely unexpected pool errors at error level.
165:     pool.on('error', (err: Error) => {
166:       const expected =
167:         err.message.includes('Connection terminated unexpectedly') ||
168:         err.message.includes('Connection ended unexpectedly') ||
169:         err.message.includes('terminating connection');
170:       if (expected) {
171:         dbLogger.debug({ pool: name, err: err.message }, 'Idle log DB connection closed by server');
172:         return;
173:       }
174:       dbLogger.error({ err, pool: name }, 'Unexpected log DB pool error');
175:     });
176:   }

178:   /**
179:    * Test connections on startup (fail-fast) and, when enabled, promote the
180:    * event tables to TimescaleDB hypertables. Safe to call once at bootstrap.
181:    */
182:   async connect(): Promise<{ primary: Date; replica?: Date }> {
183:     dbLogger.info('Testing log database connections');
184: 
185:     const primaryClient = await this.primaryPool.connect();
186:     let primaryTime: Date;
187:     try {
188:       const res = await primaryClient.query<{ time: Date; db: string }>(
189:         'SELECT NOW() AS time, current_database() AS db',
190:       );
191:       primaryTime = res.rows[0]!.time;
192:       dbLogger.info({ db: res.rows[0]?.db, time: primaryTime }, 'Log DB primary connected');
193:     } finally {
194:       primaryClient.release();
195:     }
196: 
197:     let replicaTime: Date | undefined;
198:     if (this.replicaPool) {
199:       const replicaClient = await this.replicaPool.connect();
200:       try {
201:         const replicaRes = await replicaClient.query<{ time: Date; db: string }>(
202:           'SELECT NOW() AS time, current_database() AS db',
203:         );
204:         replicaTime = replicaRes.rows[0]?.time;
205:         dbLogger.info({ db: replicaRes.rows[0]?.db, time: replicaTime }, 'Log DB replica connected');
206:       } finally {
207:         replicaClient.release();
208:       }
209:     }
210: 
211:     if (env.LOG_DB_ENABLE_TIMESCALE) {
212:       await this.initializeTimescale();
213:     }
214: 
215:     return { primary: primaryTime, ...(replicaTime ? { replica: replicaTime } : {}) };
216:   }

220:    *

223:    * tables are defined (migrations2/004), not here — that keeps DDL in one
224:    * authoritative place. This method only guarantees the extension exists so
225:    * the log DB is ready to host hypertables.

234:       const res = await client.query<{ version: string }>(
235:         `SELECT extversion AS version FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb'`,
236:       );

242:     } catch (err) {

245:         'TimescaleDB extension unavailable — log DB will run as plain PostgreSQL',
246:       );

290:    * - Non-retryable errors (constraint, permission, syntax) fail immediately.
291:    * - A per-statement timeout, when supplied, is applied via `SET LOCAL` inside
292:    *   a transaction so it can never leak onto a reused pooled connection.
293:    * - Reads default to the configured read timeout; writes default to the
294:    *   write timeout (0/unbounded) so ingestion is never aborted mid-batch.
295:    */
296:   async queryWithRetry<T extends QueryResultRow = QueryResultRow>(
297:     sql: string,
298:     params?: unknown[],
299:     options: QueryOptions = {},
300:   ): Promise<QueryResult<T>> {
301:     const { maxRetries = env.LOG_RETRIES, operation = 'read', projectId } = options;
302:     const effectiveTimeout =
303:       options.timeout ?? (operation === 'write' ? env.LOG_DB_WRITE_TIMEOUT : env.LOG_QUERY_TIMEOUT);
304: 
305:     let lastError: Error | null = null;
306: 
307:     for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++) {
308:       const client = await this.getConnection({
309:         operation,
310:         ...(projectId !== undefined ? { projectId } : {}),
311:       });
312: 
313:       try {
314:         const start = Date.now();
315:         const result = await this.runWithTimeout<T>(client, sql, params, effectiveTimeout);
316:         const duration = Date.now() - start;
317: 
318:         if (duration > env.LOG_DB_SLOW_QUERY_MS) {
319:           dbLogger.warn(
320:             { query: sql.slice(0, 120), duration, rows: result.rowCount, operation },
321:             'Slow log query detected',
322:           );
323:         }
324: 
325:         return result;
326:       } catch (err) {
327:         lastError = err as Error;
328:         const code = (err as { code?: string }).code;
329: 
330:         if (code && NON_RETRYABLE_PG_CODES.has(code)) {
331:           throw err;
332:         }
333: 
334:         const isLastAttempt = attempt === maxRetries - 1;
335:         if (!isLastAttempt) {
336:           const base = Math.min(1000 * 2 ** attempt, 5000);
337:           const delay = base + Math.floor(Math.random() * 250); // jitter
338:           dbLogger.warn(
339:             { error: (err as Error).message, code, attempt: attempt + 1, nextRetryMs: delay },
340:             'Log query failed — retrying',
341:           );
342:           await sleep(delay);
343:         }
344:       } finally {
345:         client.release();
346:       }
347:     }

657:           ORDER BY created_at ASC
658:           LIMIT $1
659:           FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED

662:           SET status = 'queued'
663:          FROM claimed

666:                   j.organization_id, j.project_id, j.alert_event_id, j.alert_key,
667:                   j.connector_id, j.route_id, j.recipient_user_id, j.recipient_ref, j.template_id,

678:     if (rows.length === 0) return 0;
679:     const result = await this.exec(client).query(
680:       `INSERT INTO alert_notification_ledger (
681:          organization_id, rule_id, rule_action_id, binding_id, alert_key,
682:          channel_kind, recipient_user_id, notification_job_id
683:        )
684:        SELECT t.organization_id, t.rule_id, t.rule_action_id, t.binding_id, t.alert_key,
685:               t.channel_kind::notification_channel_kind, t.recipient_user_id, t.notification_job_id
686:          FROM UNNEST(
687:            $1::uuid[], $2::uuid[], $3::uuid[], $4::uuid[], $5::text[],
688:            $6::text[], $7::uuid[], $8::uuid[]
689:          ) AS t(organization_id, rule_id, rule_action_id, binding_id, alert_key,
690:                 channel_kind, recipient_user_id, notification_job_id)`,
691:       [
692:         rows.map((r) => r.organizationId),
693:         rows.map((r) => r.ruleId ?? null),
694:         rows.map((r) => r.ruleActionId ?? null),
695:         rows.map((r) => r.bindingId ?? null),
696:         rows.map((r) => r.alertKey),
697:         rows.map((r) => r.channelKind),
698:         rows.map((r) => r.recipientUserId ?? null),
699:         rows.map((r) => r.notificationJobId ?? null),
700:       ],
701:     );
702:     return result.rowCount ?? 0;
703:   }

705:   /**
706:    * Derive throttle state for rule actions from the append-only ledger.
707:    *
708:    * Replaces reading the old mutable `alert_throttle_windows` row (audit A3): one
709:    * grouped query returns both the per-window count and the last notification time,
710:    * which is everything the throttle predicate needs.
711:    */
712:   async getThrottleWindowStates(
713:     ruleActionIds: string[],
714:     windowSeconds: number,
715:     client?: PoolClient,
716:   ): Promise<ThrottleWindowState[]> {
717:     if (ruleActionIds.length === 0) return [];
718:     const result = await this.exec(client).query<{
719:       rule_action_id: string;
720:       notification_count: string;
721:       last_notified_at: Date | null;
722:     }>(
723:       `SELECT rule_action_id,
724:               COUNT(*)::text AS notification_count,
725:               MAX(notified_at) AS last_notified_at
726:          FROM alert_notification_ledger
727:         WHERE rule_action_id = ANY($1::uuid[])
728:           AND notified_at > now() - ($2::bigint * INTERVAL '1 second')
729:         GROUP BY rule_action_id`,
730:       [ruleActionIds, Math.max(1, Math.floor(windowSeconds))],
731:     );
732:     return result.rows.map((row) => ({
733:       ruleActionId: row.rule_action_id,
734:       notificationCount: Number(row.notification_count),
735:       lastNotifiedAt: row.last_notified_at,
736:     }));
737:   }

751:              $6::uuid[], $7::uuid[], $8::uuid[], $9::smallint[], $10::text[],
752:              $11::int[], $12::text[], $13::text[], $14::text[], $15::int[]
753:            ) AS t(organization_id, project_id, alert_event_id, notification_job_id, channel_kind,
754:                   connector_id, route_id, recipient_user_id, attempt_number, status,
755:                   response_status_code, external_message_id, error_category, error_message, latency_ms)
756:        ), reserved AS (
757:          INSERT INTO alert_runtime_idempotency_keys (namespace, organization_id, idempotency_key)
758:          SELECT 'delivery_attempt', organization_id,
759:                 notification_job_id::text || ':' || attempt_number::text
760:            FROM input
761:          ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
762:          RETURNING organization_id, idempotency_key
763:        )
764:        INSERT INTO alert_delivery_attempts_v2 (
765:          organization_id, project_id, alert_event_id, notification_job_id, channel_kind,
766:          connector_id, route_id, recipient_user_id, attempt_number, status,
767:          response_status_code, external_message_id, error_category, error_message, latency_ms
768:        )
769:        SELECT t.organization_id, t.project_id, t.alert_event_id, t.notification_job_id,
770:               t.channel_kind::notification_channel_kind,

772:               t.status::notification_job_status,
773:               t.response_status_code, t.external_message_id, t.error_category,
774:               t.error_message, t.latency_ms
775:          FROM input t

106:            action, entity_type, entity_id, entity_name, request_id, http_method, endpoint,
107:            new_values, status, metadata
108:          ) VALUES (
109:            $1, $2, $3, $4::inet, $5, $6::uuid,
110:            'organization.created', 'organization', $1, $7, $8::uuid, $9, $10,

118:           JSON.stringify({ source: 'organization.create' }),
119:         ],

70:  * Build the frontend invite-accept URL. `accountExists` lets the frontend
71:  * decide which screen to show: sign-in (existing user) vs. create-account
72:  * (brand-new invitee). The base is FRONTEND_URL, falling back to APP_URL.
73:  */
74: function buildInviteUrl(token: string, accountExists: boolean): string {
75:   const base = (env.FRONTEND_URL || env.APP_URL || "").replace(/\/+$/, "");
76:   const params = new URLSearchParams({
77:     token,
78:     accountExists: accountExists ? "true" : "false",
79:   });
80:   return `${base}/invite?${params.toString()}`;
81: }

433: /**
434:  * Resolve the user id recorded as `created_by` for seeded rules: the org
435:  * owner (organizations.owner_user_id), falling back to the first active
436:  * owner/admin member. Returns null when the org has no resolvable owner —
437:  * the caller then skips seeding for that org (alert_rules.created_by is
438:  * NOT NULL with a users FK, so we cannot seed without one).
439:  */
440: async function resolvePresetActor(pool: Pool, orgId: string): Promise<string | null> {
441:   const owner = await pool.query<{ owner_user_id: string }>(
442:     `SELECT owner_user_id FROM organizations WHERE id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL`,
443:     [orgId],
444:   );
445:   if (owner.rows[0]) return owner.rows[0].owner_user_id;
446: 
447:   const member = await pool.query<{ user_id: string }>(
448:     `SELECT user_id
449:      FROM organization_members
450:      WHERE org_id = $1 AND status = 'active' AND role IN ('owner', 'admin')
451:      ORDER BY CASE role WHEN 'owner' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, joined_at ASC NULLS LAST
452:      LIMIT 1`,
453:     [orgId],
454:   );
455:   return member.rows[0]?.user_id ?? null;
456: }
457: 
458: /**
459:  * Seed any missing default presets for an org (org-level, project_id NULL).
460:  * Idempotent: `uq_alert_rules_preset_scope` (partial unique index on
461:  * (organization_id, project_id, preset_key) NULLS NOT DISTINCT) plus
462:  * ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING make re-runs safe, including concurrent ones.
463:  * Returns the number of presets actually inserted.
464:  *
465:  * Exported for the org-creation/provisioning flow AND invoked from the
466:  * evaluator tick for orgs that already have traffic but no presets yet.
467:  */
468: export async function seedDefaultPresetsForOrg(pool: Pool, orgId: string): Promise<number> {
469:   const createdBy = await resolvePresetActor(pool, orgId);
470:   if (!createdBy) return 0;
471: 
472:   const client = await pool.connect();
473:   try {
474:     await client.query('BEGIN');
475:     let seeded = 0;
476:     for (const preset of DEFAULT_ALERT_PRESETS) {
477:       const inserted = await client.query<{ id: string }>(
478:         `INSERT INTO alert_rules
479:            (organization_id, name, description, severity, enabled,
480:             evaluation_interval_seconds, cooldown_seconds, auto_resolve_after_minutes,
481:             deduplication_window_seconds,

I’m refactoring the preset seeding into a client-aware helper, then invoking it from the existing workspace provisioning transaction with the authenticated organization owner as `created_by`.

1: /**
2:  * Escalation sweep worker.
3:  *
4:  * Wires the previously schema-only escalation model into a live execution path:
5:  *
6:  *   1. Expired acknowledgments flip back to `firing` so escalation resumes.
7:  *   2. Firing events whose `next_escalation_at` is due are claimed with
8:  *      FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (no two workers process the same event).
9:  *   3. The next active step of the event's policy is executed: connector-send
10:  *      jobs are enqueued for the step's connectors/routes, the event advances
11:  *      to that step, and the following step's wait schedules the next run.
12:  *   4. When steps run out, the policy's repeat config decides: repeat from
13:  *      step 1 (bounded by max_repeats; 0 = unlimited) or stop escalating.
14:  *
15:  * All escalation transitions write `alert_event_history` rows for audit.
16:  */
17: import type { FastifyBaseLogger } from 'fastify';
18: import type { AlertingRepository } from './repository.js';
19: import type { ConnectorRepository } from '../connectors/repository.js';
20: import type { ConnectorConfigRow, NotificationPayload, NotificationSeverity } from '../connectors/types.js';
21: import { CONNECTOR_JOBS, CONNECTOR_PRIORITY, type ConnectorJobName } from '../connectors/job.constants.js';
22: import type { AlertEscalationStepRow, AlertEventRow } from './types.js';
23: import { env } from '../../config/env.js';
24: 
25: type EnqueueConnectorJob = (
26:   queue: ConnectorJobName,
27:   data: Record<string, unknown>,
28:   options?: Record<string, unknown>,
29: ) => Promise<unknown>;
30: 
31: export interface EscalationSweepResult {
32:   resumedAcknowledgments: number;
33:   claimed: number;
34:   escalated: number;
35:   repeated: number;
36:   exhausted: number;
37:   failed: number;
38: }
39: 
40: export class AlertEscalationSweep {
41:   constructor(
42:     private readonly alertRepo: AlertingRepository,
43:     private readonly connectorRepo: ConnectorRepository,
44:     private readonly enqueueConnectorJob: EnqueueConnectorJob,
45:     private readonly logger: FastifyBaseLogger,
46:   ) {}
47: 
48:   async run(limit: number): Promise<EscalationSweepResult> {
49:     const log = this.logger.child({ component: 'escalation-sweep' });
50:     const result: EscalationSweepResult = {
51:       resumedAcknowledgments: 0, claimed: 0, escalated: 0, repeated: 0, exhausted: 0, failed: 0,
52:     };
53: 
54:     // 1. Expired acknowledgments resume escalation.
55:     const resumed = await this.alertRepo.resumeExpiredAcknowledgments(limit);
56:     result.resumedAcknowledgments = resumed.length;
57:     await Promise.allSettled(resumed.map((event) => this.alertRepo.insertHistory({
58:       eventId: event.id, organizationId: event.organization_id,
59:       action: 'requeued', actorId: null, actorType: 'worker',
60:       newState: { status: 'firing' },
61:       metadata: { reason: 'acknowledgment_expired' },
62:     })));
63: 
64:     // 2. Claim due escalations (SKIP LOCKED inside the repository).
65:     const events = await this.alertRepo.claimEscalationDue(limit);
66:     result.claimed = events.length;
67:     if (events.length === 0) return result;
68: 
69:     // 3. Bulk-load policies, steps, and connectors (no N+1).
70:     const policyIds = [...new Set(events.map((e) => e.escalation_policy_id).filter((id): id is string => id !== null))];
71:     const policies = await Promise.all(
72:       policyIds.map((id) => this.alertRepo.findEscalationPolicy(events.find((e) => e.escalation_policy_id === id)!.organization_id, id)),
73:     );
74:     const policyById = new Map(policies.filter((p) => p !== null).map((p) => [p!.id, p!]));
75: 
76:     const steps = await this.alertRepo.listEscalationStepsByPolicyIds(policyIds);
77:     const stepsByPolicyId = new Map<string, AlertEscalationStepRow[]>();
78:     for (const step of steps) {
79:       const list = stepsByPolicyId.get(step.policy_id) ?? [];
80:       list.push(step);
81:       stepsByPolicyId.set(step.policy_id, list);
82:     }
83: 
84:     const connectorIds = [...new Set(steps.flatMap((s) => s.connector_ids))];
85:     const connectors = await this.connectorRepo.getByIds(connectorIds);
86:     const connectorById = new Map<string, ConnectorConfigRow>(connectors.map((c) => [c.id, c]));
87: 
88:     // 4. Advance each event concurrently; one failure never aborts the sweep.
89:     const settled = await Promise.allSettled(events.map(async (event) => {
90:       const policy = event.escalation_policy_id ? policyById.get(event.escalation_policy_id) : undefined;
91:       const policySteps = event.escalation_policy_id ? stepsByPolicyId.get(event.escalation_policy_id) ?? [] : [];
92:       await this.advanceEvent(event, policy ?? null, policySteps, connectorById, result);
93:     }));
94: 
95:     settled.forEach((res, i) => {
96:       if (res.status === 'rejected') {
97:         result.failed += 1;
98:         log.error({ err: res.reason, eventId: events[i]!.id }, 'Escalation advance failed');
99:       }
100:     });
101: 
102:     if (result.claimed > 0 || result.resumedAcknowledgments > 0) {
103:       log.info({ ...result }, 'Escalation sweep finished');
104:     }
105:     return result;
106:   }
107: 
108:   private async advanceEvent(
109:     event: AlertEventRow,
110:     policy: { repeat_interval_minutes: number | null; max_repeats: number; is_active: boolean } | null,
111:     steps: AlertEscalationStepRow[],
112:     connectorById: Map<string, ConnectorConfigRow>,
113:     result: EscalationSweepResult,
114:   ): Promise<void> {
115:     const nextStep = steps.find((s) => s.step_number > event.escalation_step_number);
116: 
117:     if (policy && policy.is_active && nextStep) {

120:       const followingStep = steps.find((s) => s.step_number > nextStep.step_number);
121:       let nextAt: Date | null = null;
122:       let stepNumber = nextStep.step_number;
123:       let repeatCount = event.escalation_repeat_count;
124: 
125:       if (followingStep) {
126:         nextAt = new Date(Date.now() + followingStep.wait_minutes * 60_000);
127:       } else if (this.canRepeat(policy, repeatCount)) {
128:         // No more steps — wrap around to step 1 after the repeat interval.
129:         stepNumber = 0;
130:         repeatCount += 1;
131:         nextAt = new Date(Date.now() + (policy.repeat_interval_minutes ?? 0) * 60_000);
132:         result.repeated += 1;
133:       }
134: 
135:       await this.alertRepo.advanceEscalation(event.id, stepNumber, repeatCount, nextAt);
136:       await this.alertRepo.insertHistory({
137:         eventId: event.id, organizationId: event.organization_id,
138:         action: 'escalation_step', actorId: null, actorType: 'worker',
139:         newState: { escalationStepNumber: nextStep.step_number, repeatCount },
140:         metadata: { policyId: event.escalation_policy_id },

143:       return;
144:     }
145: 
146:     // No further step and no repeat (or policy gone/inactive) — stop escalating.
147:     if (policy && policy.is_active && steps.length > 0 && this.canRepeat(policy, event.escalation_repeat_count)) {
148:       const firstStep = steps[0]!;
149:       await this.executeStep(event, firstStep, connectorById);
150:       await this.alertRepo.advanceEscalation(
151:         event.id, 0, event.escalation_repeat_count + 1,
152:         new Date(Date.now() + (policy.repeat_interval_minutes ?? 0) * 60_000),
153:       );
154:       await this.alertRepo.insertHistory({
155:         eventId: event.id, organizationId: event.organization_id,
156:         action: 'escalation_step', actorId: null, actorType: 'worker',
157:         newState: { escalationStepNumber: firstStep.step_number, repeatCount: event.escalation_repeat_count + 1 },
158:         metadata: { policyId: event.escalation_policy_id, repeat: true },
159:       });
160:       result.repeated += 1;
161:       return;
162:     }
163: 
164:     await this.alertRepo.advanceEscalation(event.id, event.escalation_step_number, event.escalation_repeat_count, null);
165:     await this.alertRepo.insertHistory({
166:       eventId: event.id, organizationId: event.organization_id,
167:       action: 'escalated', actorId: null, actorType: 'worker',
168:       newState: { escalationExhausted: true },
169:       metadata: { policyId: event.escalation_policy_id },
170:     });
171:     result.exhausted += 1;
172:   }
173: 
174:   private canRepeat(
175:     policy: { repeat_interval_minutes: number | null; max_repeats: number },
176:     repeatCount: number,
177:   ): boolean {
178:     if (policy.repeat_interval_minutes === null || policy.repeat_interval_minutes <= 0) return false;
179:     return policy.max_repeats === 0 || repeatCount < policy.max_repeats;

57:   constructor(logger: FastifyBaseLogger, telemetryPool: Pool = pool, dryRun?: boolean) {

65:   async runTick(limit = 500): Promise<ProjectThresholdTickSummary> {
66:     const summary: ProjectThresholdTickSummary = { due: 0, evaluated: 0, fired: 0, recovered: 0, failed: 0 };
67:     let due: EvaluatedThresholdRow[];
68:     try {
69:       due = await this.findDue(limit);

72:       this.log.error({ err }, "Unable to load due project thresholds");

82:       }
83:       summary.evaluated += result.value === "unsupported" ? 0 : 1;
84:       if (result.value === "fired") summary.fired += 1;
85:       if (result.value === "recovered") summary.recovered += 1;
86:     });
87:     return summary;
88:   }

102:           AND environment.organization_id = threshold.organization_id

105:           AND (threshold.environment_id IS NULL

107:           AND (threshold.last_evaluated_at IS NULL

109:                     + threshold.evaluation_window_minutes * INTERVAL '1 minute' <= NOW())
110:         ORDER BY threshold.last_evaluated_at ASC NULLS FIRST, threshold.id
111:         LIMIT $1`,
112:       [Math.max(1, Math.min(limit, 1000))],
113:     );
114:     return result.rows;
115:   }

import type { FastifyBaseLogger } from "fastify";
import type { Pool } from "pg";
import { pool } from "../../../../config/database.js";
import { AlertingRepository } from "../../../alerting/repository.js";
import { EventsService } from "../../../alerting/events/events.service.js";
import { compareThreshold } from "./threshold.evaluator.js";
import type { ProjectAlertThresholdRow } from "./threshold.types.js";

interface EvaluatedThresholdRow extends ProjectAlertThresholdRow {
  current_breaches: number;
  is_breaching: boolean;
  last_evaluated_at: Date | null;
}

export interface ProjectThresholdTickSummary {
  due: number;
  evaluated: number;
  fired: number;
  recovered: number;
  failed: number;
}

type ThresholdOutcome = "fired" | "recovered" | "breaching" | "clear" | "cooldown" | "unsupported";

const METRIC_EXPRESSIONS: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  total_events: "COALESCE(SUM(total_events),0)::float8",
  errors: "COALESCE(SUM(errors),0)::float8",
  ingestion_errors: "COALESCE(SUM(errors),0)::float8",
  requests: "COALESCE(SUM(requests),0)::float8",
  failed_notifications: "COALESCE(SUM(failed_notifications),0)::float8",
  rate_limit_usage: "COALESCE(SUM(rate_limit_usage),0)::float8",
  // Latency percentiles are intentionally absent: percentiles are not
  // composable across buckets, so they cannot be derived from additive usage
  // rollups. Latency SLOs must be evaluated by a mergeable-sketch pipeline.
};

export class ProjectThresholdWorker {
  private readonly repository: AlertingRepository;
  private readonly events: EventsService;
  private readonly log: FastifyBaseLogger;
  /**
   * Pool that owns TELEMETRY (`events_*`). ADR-0006 / DEV-002.
   *
   * Only the apdex metric reads telemetry. `project_usage_minute`, `ai_usage_logs`,
   * `project_alert_thresholds` and `alert_events` are control-plane owned and stay on the
   * primary pool. Defaults to the primary pool so single-database deployments are unchanged.
   */
  private readonly telemetry: Pool;
  /** When true, thresholds are evaluated and logged but no alert is emitted or resolved. */
  private readonly dryRun: boolean;

  /**
   * @param telemetryPool pool owning `events_*`; defaults to the control-plane pool
   * @param dryRun explicit override supplied by AlertRuleEvaluator. Defaults to "dry-run if the
   *   telemetry pool is a different pool", so single-database deployments are unaffected.
   */
  constructor(logger: FastifyBaseLogger, telemetryPool: Pool = pool, dryRun?: boolean) {
    this.repository = new AlertingRepository();
    this.events = new EventsService({ repository: this.repository, logger });
    this.log = logger.child({ component: "project-threshold-evaluator" });
    this.telemetry = telemetryPool;
    this.dryRun = dryRun ?? this.telemetry !== pool;
  }

  async runTick(limit = 500): Promise<ProjectThresholdTickSummary> {
    const summary: ProjectThresholdTickSummary = { due: 0, evaluated: 0, fired: 0, recovered: 0, failed: 0 };
    let due: EvaluatedThresholdRow[];
    try {
      due = await this.findDue(limit);
    } catch (err) {
      summary.failed = 1;
      this.log.error({ err }, "Unable to load due project thresholds");
      return summary;
    }
    summary.due = due.length;
    const settled = await mapBounded(due, 10, (threshold) => this.evaluateOne(threshold));
    settled.forEach((result, index) => {
      if (result.status === "rejected") {
        summary.failed += 1;
        this.log.error({ err: result.reason, thresholdId: due[index]?.id }, "Project threshold evaluation failed");
        return;
      }
      summary.evaluated += result.value === "unsupported" ? 0 : 1;
      if (result.value === "fired") summary.fired += 1;
      if (result.value === "recovered") summary.recovered += 1;
    });
    return summary;
  }

  private async findDue(limit: number): Promise<EvaluatedThresholdRow[]> {
    const result = await pool.query<EvaluatedThresholdRow>(
      `SELECT threshold.*
         FROM project_alert_thresholds threshold
         JOIN projects project
           ON project.id = threshold.project_id
          AND project.org_id = threshold.organization_id
          AND project.status = 'active'
          AND project.deleted_at IS NULL
         LEFT JOIN project_environments environment
           ON environment.id = threshold.environment_id
          AND environment.project_id = threshold.project_id
          AND environment.organization_id = threshold.organization_id
        WHERE threshold.enabled = TRUE
          AND threshold.deleted_at IS NULL
          AND (threshold.environment_id IS NULL
               OR (environment.is_active = TRUE AND environment.deleted_at IS NULL))
          AND (threshold.last_evaluated_at IS NULL
               OR threshold.last_evaluated_at
                    + threshold.evaluation_window_minutes * INTERVAL '1 minute' <= NOW())
        ORDER BY threshold.last_evaluated_at ASC NULLS FIRST, threshold.id
        LIMIT $1`,
      [Math.max(1, Math.min(limit, 1000))],
    );
    return result.rows;
  }

  private async evaluateOne(threshold: EvaluatedThresholdRow): Promise<ThresholdOutcome> {
    const actual = await this.readMetric(threshold);
    if (actual === null) {
      await this.markEvaluated(threshold, 0, false, false, false);
      this.log.debug({ thresholdId: threshold.id, metric: threshold.metric_name }, "Unsupported project threshold metric");
      return "unsupported";
    }

    const matched = compareThreshold(
      actual,
      threshold.comparison_operator,
      Number(threshold.threshold_value),
    );
    const breaches = matched ? threshold.current_breaches + 1 : 0;
    const reached = matched && breaches >= threshold.consecutive_breaches;
    const cooldownElapsed = !threshold.last_triggered_at
      || threshold.last_triggered_at.getTime() + threshold.cooldown_minutes * 60_000 <= Date.now();
    const shouldFire = reached && cooldownElapsed;
    const shouldRecover = !matched && threshold.is_breaching;

    // DEV-002 dry-run: evaluate and record breach state, but never emit or auto-resolve.
    if (this.dryRun) {
      if (shouldFire || shouldRecover) {
        this.log.warn(
          {
            thresholdId: threshold.id,
            projectId: threshold.project_id,
            thresholdKey: threshold.threshold_key,
            metric: threshold.metric_name,
            actual,
            threshold: Number(threshold.threshold_value),
            intent: shouldFire ? "fire" : "recover",
          },
          "DRY-RUN: project threshold would have emitted an alert (no alert event created)",
        );
      }
      await this.markEvaluated(threshold, breaches, reached, false, false);
      if (shouldFire) return "fired";
      if (shouldRecover) return "recovered";
      if (reached) return "cooldown";
      return matched ? "breaching" : "clear";
    }

    if (shouldFire) await this.emit(threshold, actual, false);
    if (shouldRecover) {
      await this.resolveActiveEvents(threshold);
      if (threshold.notify_on_recovery) await this.emit(threshold, actual, true);
    }
    await this.markEvaluated(threshold, breaches, reached, shouldFire, shouldRecover);

    if (shouldFire) return "fired";
    if (shouldRecover) return "recovered";
    if (reached) return "cooldown";
    return matched ? "breaching" : "clear";
  }

  private async readMetric(threshold: EvaluatedThresholdRow): Promise<number | null> {
    if (threshold.metric_name === "error_rate" || threshold.threshold_key === "ingestion_error_rate") {
      return this.readUsageExpression(
        threshold,
        "CASE WHEN SUM(requests)>0 THEN 100.0*SUM(errors)/SUM(requests) ELSE 0 END::float8",
      );
    }
    if (threshold.threshold_key === "rate_limit_usage") {
      return this.readUsageExpression(
        threshold,
        "CASE WHEN SUM(requests)+SUM(rate_limit_usage)>0 THEN 100.0*SUM(rate_limit_usage)/(SUM(requests)+SUM(rate_limit_usage)) ELSE 0 END::float8",
      );
    }
    if (threshold.metric_name === "apdex") {
      // Telemetry read (events_requests) → telemetry pool (ADR-0006 / DEV-002).
      const result = await this.telemetry.query<{ value: number | null }>(
        `SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>0 THEN
           (COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE latency_ms<=500)
             + 0.5*COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE latency_ms>500 AND latency_ms<=2000))/COUNT(*)
          ELSE NULL END::float8 AS value
         FROM events_requests
        WHERE organization_id=$1 AND project_id=$2
          AND occurred_at>=NOW()-($3::int*INTERVAL '1 minute')`,
        [threshold.organization_id, threshold.project_id, threshold.evaluation_window_minutes],
      );
      return result.rows[0]?.value ?? null;
    }
    if (threshold.metric_name === "ai_cost") {
      const result = await pool.query<{ value: number }>(
        `SELECT COALESCE(SUM(estimated_cost_usd),0)::float8 AS value
           FROM ai_usage_logs
          WHERE organization_id=$1 AND project_id=$2
            AND occurred_at>=NOW()-($3::int*INTERVAL '1 minute')`,
        [threshold.organization_id, threshold.project_id, threshold.evaluation_window_minutes],
      );
      return Number(result.rows[0]?.value ?? 0);
    }
    if (threshold.threshold_key === "event_volume_spike" || threshold.threshold_key === "event_volume_drop") {
      const result = await pool.query<{ value: number }>(
        `WITH windows AS (
           SELECT COALESCE(SUM(total_events) FILTER(
                    WHERE bucket>=NOW()-($3::int*INTERVAL '1 minute')),0)::float8 current_value,
                  COALESCE(SUM(total_events) FILTER(
                    WHERE bucket<NOW()-($3::int*INTERVAL '1 minute')),0)::float8 previous_value
             FROM project_usage_minute
            WHERE organization_id=$1 AND project_id=$2
              AND bucket>=NOW()-(2*$3::int*INTERVAL '1 minute')
              AND ($4::uuid IS NULL OR environment_id=$4)
         ) SELECT CASE WHEN previous_value>0
                  THEN 100.0*current_value/previous_value ELSE 0 END::float8 AS value
             FROM windows`,
        [threshold.organization_id, threshold.project_id, threshold.evaluation_window_minutes, threshold.environment_id],
      );
      return Number(result.rows[0]?.value ?? 0);
    }
    if (threshold.threshold_key === "failed_notification_rate") {
      return this.readUsageExpression(
        threshold,
        "CASE WHEN SUM(connector_deliveries)>0 THEN 100.0*SUM(failed_notifications)/SUM(connector_deliveries) ELSE 0 END::float8",
      );
    }
    const expression = METRIC_EXPRESSIONS[threshold.metric_name];
    return expression ? this.readUsageExpression(threshold, expression) : null;
  }

  private async readUsageExpression(threshold: EvaluatedThresholdRow, expression: string): Promise<number> {
    const result = await pool.query<{ value: number }>(
      `SELECT ${expression} AS value
         FROM project_usage_minute
        WHERE organization_id=$1 AND project_id=$2
          AND bucket>=NOW()-($3::int*INTERVAL '1 minute')
          AND ($4::uuid IS NULL OR environment_id=$4)`,
      [threshold.organization_id, threshold.project_id, threshold.evaluation_window_minutes, threshold.environment_id],
    );
    return Number(result.rows[0]?.value ?? 0);
  }

  private async emit(threshold: EvaluatedThresholdRow, actual: number, recovery: boolean): Promise<void> {
    await this.events.ingestEvent(threshold.organization_id, {
      projectId: threshold.project_id,
      severity: recovery ? "info" : this.severity(threshold.severity),
      source: "project-threshold-evaluator",
      fingerprint: `project-threshold:${threshold.id}`,
      payload: {
        title: recovery ? `Recovered: ${threshold.threshold_key}` : `Threshold breached: ${threshold.threshold_key}`,
        message: recovery
          ? `${threshold.metric_name} recovered to ${actual}`
          : `${threshold.metric_name} ${threshold.comparison_operator} ${threshold.threshold_value} (actual ${actual})`,
        projectId: threshold.project_id,
        environmentId: threshold.environment_id,
        category: threshold.category,
        metric: threshold.metric_name,
        actual,
        threshold: Number(threshold.threshold_value),
        unit: threshold.threshold_unit,
        recovery,
      },
      labels: {
        project_id: threshold.project_id,
        threshold_id: threshold.id,
        category: threshold.category,
        ...(threshold.environment_id ? { environment_id: threshold.environment_id } : {}),
      },
      annotations: {
        thresholdKey: threshold.threshold_key,
        evaluatedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
      },
    });
  }

  private async resolveActiveEvents(threshold: EvaluatedThresholdRow): Promise<void> {
    const active = await pool.query<{ id: string }>(
      `SELECT id FROM alert_events
        WHERE organization_id=$1 AND project_id=$2 AND fingerprint=$3
          AND status IN ('firing','acknowledged','pending','processing')
        ORDER BY started_at DESC
        LIMIT 50`,
      [threshold.organization_id, threshold.project_id, `project-threshold:${threshold.id}`],
    );
    for (const row of active.rows) {
      await this.repository.resolveEvent(threshold.organization_id, row.id, null, "auto", true);
      await this.repository.insertHistory({
        eventId: row.id,
        organizationId: threshold.organization_id,
        action: "auto_resolved",
        actorId: null,
        actorType: "worker",
        metadata: { reason: "project_threshold_recovered", thresholdId: threshold.id },
      });
    }
  }

  private severity(value: string): "info" | "warning" | "error" | "critical" {
    return value === "info" || value === "warning" || value === "error" || value === "critical"
      ? value
      : "warning";
  }

  private async markEvaluated(
    threshold: EvaluatedThresholdRow,
    breaches: number,
    isBreaching: boolean,
    fired: boolean,
    recovered: boolean,
  ): Promise<void> {
    await pool.query(
      `UPDATE project_alert_thresholds
          SET current_breaches=$2,
              is_breaching=$3,
              last_evaluated_at=NOW(),
              last_triggered_at=CASE WHEN $4 THEN NOW() ELSE last_triggered_at END,
              last_recovered_at=CASE WHEN $5 THEN NOW() ELSE last_recovered_at END,
              updated_at=NOW(), version=version+1
        WHERE id=$1 AND organization_id=$6 AND project_id=$7
          AND enabled=TRUE AND deleted_at IS NULL`,
      [
        threshold.id,
        breaches,
        isBreaching,
        fired,
        recovered,
        threshold.organization_id,
        threshold.project_id,
      ],
    );
  }
}

async function mapBounded<T, R>(
  items: T[],
  limit: number,
  task: (item: T) => Promise<R>,
): Promise<PromiseSettledResult<R>[]> {
  const results: PromiseSettledResult<R>[] = new Array(items.length);
  let cursor = 0;
  const lane = async (): Promise<void> => {
    while (cursor < items.length) {
      const index = cursor++;
      try {
        results[index] = { status: "fulfilled", value: await task(items[index]!) };
      } catch (reason) {
        results[index] = { status: "rejected", reason };
      }
    }
  };
  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(limit, items.length) }, lane));
  return results;
}

<details>
<summary><em>Thinking</em></summary>

> ***Evaluating integration options***
>
> *I'm noticing that the NotificationRoutingService is using AlertConfigRepository, which is good, but there's a major issue with AlertRuntimeEngines not leveraging AlertDecisionEngine as planned. The existing runtime engine continues to directly append events and jobs. This makes me think—should I update AlertRuntimeEngines to use the decision engine? There’s potential for integration, but the decision engine also has its own state and cooldown. Maybe we should focus on centralizing through AlertDecisionEngine to eliminate duplicate jobs and states. It's a lot to consider!**Considering routing service integration***
>
> *I'm evaluating that the transaction and control-plane routing service can be called inside the log transaction, which reads from the control DB, but doesn't handle transactions across databases. This service can accept optional routing and utilize labels, allowing runtime engines to potentially call the decisionEngine. However, the engines are using `AlertRuntimeRepository` for evaluation state, not the decision engine. I think a larger refactor might be necessary, but it seems doable. I’ll need to ensure proper tests are in place as well.**Reviewing code and migration plans***
>
> *I'm checking the code for a job insertion issue called outside a runtime transaction, which separates queries that need shared transactions. The plan speaks of a canonical boundary that we should look to improve. I might start by inspecting git diffs for odd modifications, focusing on specific files. The user mentioned continuing concisely, so I need to keep that in mind. We have existing todos about config migration and possibly marking that complete, but some aspects, like the legacy threshold API, need more work.**Considering refactoring and implementation***
>
> *I'm thinking about implementing a facade, but it feels substantial. Before diving in, I should make a refactor decision. It might be useful to check the existing runtime tests to see if there's a lack of integration. I should probably run `git diff -- src` to focus on the specific changes in the source code. This way, I can understand what’s happening in the codebase before making any major moves. Let's take it one step at a time!*

</details>

The acceptance suite is green: 49 tests pass, strict TypeScript passes, and whitespace validation is clean. I’m reviewing the source diff now because the build regenerated ignored/compiled artifacts again, and I want to catch any architectural mismatch—especially the remaining duplicate V2 decision logic—before I proceed with API compatibility work.

+function categoryForRule(conditions: AlertRuleConditionRow[], source: string): string {
+  const fieldPath = conditions[0]?.field_path?.toLowerCase() ?? '';
+  if (fieldPath.startsWith('security') || fieldPath.includes('auth')) return 'security';
+  if (fieldPath.startsWith('deployment')) return 'deployment';
+  if (fieldPath.startsWith('cron')) return 'cron';
+  if (fieldPath.startsWith('ai.')) return 'ai';
+  if (fieldPath.includes('latency') || fieldPath.includes('availability') || fieldPath.includes('error')) return 'performance';
+  if (source.includes('billing')) return 'billing';
+  return 'all';
+}
+
+function toRoutingSeverity(severity: LogDbSeverity): 'info' | 'warning' | 'error' | 'critical' {
+  if (severity === 'critical' || severity === 'fatal') return 'critical';
+  if (severity === 'error') return 'error';
+  if (severity === 'warning') return 'warning';
+  return 'info';
 }

+export async function seedDefaultPresetsForOrgInTransaction(

+): Promise<number> {
+  let seeded = 0;
+  for (const preset of DEFAULT_ALERT_PRESETS) {
+    const inserted = await client.query<{ id: string }>(
+      `INSERT INTO alert_rules
+         (organization_id, name, description, severity, enabled,
+          evaluation_interval_seconds, cooldown_seconds, auto_resolve_after_minutes,
+          deduplication_window_seconds,
+          labels, annotations, metadata, created_by, enabled_at,
+          project_id, preset_key, is_default)
+       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, TRUE, $5, $6, $7, $8, $9, $10, $11, $12, NOW(),
+               NULL, $13, TRUE)
+       ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
+       RETURNING id`,
+      [
+        orgId,
+        preset.name,
+        preset.description,
+        preset.severity,
+        preset.evaluationIntervalSeconds,
+        preset.cooldownSeconds,
+        preset.autoResolveAfterMinutes,
+        preset.deduplicationWindowSeconds,
+        JSON.stringify({ preset: true }),
+        JSON.stringify({ preset_key: preset.presetKey }),
+        JSON.stringify(preset.metadata ?? {}),
+        createdBy,
+        preset.presetKey,
+      ],
+    );
+    const rule = inserted.rows[0];
+    if (!rule) continue;
+
+    await client.query(
+      `INSERT INTO alert_rule_conditions
+         (rule_id, condition_type, field_path, operator, threshold_value,
+          lookback_minutes, aggregate_function, is_required, order_index)
+       VALUES ($1, 'threshold'::alert_condition_type, $2, $3::alert_condition_operator,
+               $4, $5, $6, TRUE, 0)`,
+      [
+        rule.id,
+        preset.condition.fieldPath,
+        preset.condition.operator,
+        JSON.stringify(preset.condition.thresholdValue ?? null),
+        preset.condition.lookbackMinutes,
+        preset.condition.aggregateFunction ?? null,
+      ],
+    );
+
+    await client.query(
+      `INSERT INTO alert_rule_actions
+         (rule_id, action_type, priority, order_index, action_conditions, is_active)
+       VALUES ($1, 'notify'::alert_action_type, 100, 0, $2, TRUE)`,
+      [rule.id, JSON.stringify({ channel: 'in_app', audience: 'project_members' })],
+    );
+    seeded += 1;
+  }
+  return seeded;

The diff review found two correctness gaps before I move on: the new V2 job metadata fields are not yet populated by the job builder, and ledger entries are discarding recipient user IDs even though the job contract now carries them. I’m fixing those first, then I’ll gate legacy batch registration and inspect whether claimed legacy escalation rows are safely reprocessed after V2 filtering.

583: /**
584:  * Claim pending events (in batches of 100) for orgs that have any, and enqueue
585:  * a process-batch job per batch. Bounded by `maxBatches` per run to avoid
586:  * starving other queues. The pg-boss job id is recorded on the batch for
587:  * dead-letter traceability.
588:  */
589: async function formBatches(
590:   alertRepo: AlertingRepository,
591:   log: FastifyBaseLogger,
592:   maxBatches: number,
593:   onlyOrgId?: string,
594: ): Promise<number> {
595:   const orgIds = onlyOrgId ? [onlyOrgId] : await alertRepo.findOrgsWithPendingEvents(maxBatches);
596:   if (orgIds.length === 0) return 0;
597: 
598:   let formed = 0;
599:   const perOrgCap = Math.max(1, Math.floor(maxBatches / orgIds.length)); // fair share
600:   await Promise.all(orgIds.map(async (orgId) => {
601:     const workerId = `former-${process.pid}`;
602:     for (let i = 0; i < perOrgCap; i++) {
603:       const batch = await alertRepo.createBatchFromPending(orgId, BATCH_SIZE, workerId);
604:       if (!batch) break; // org drained
605:       const jobId = await pgboss.send(ALERT_JOBS.processBatch,
606:         { batchId: batch.id, organizationId: orgId } satisfies BatchJobData,
607:         { retryLimit: 3, retryDelay: 60, retryBackoff: true, expireInSeconds: 7200 } as never);
608:       await alertRepo.setBatchJobId(batch.id, typeof jobId === 'string' ? jobId : null);
609:       formed += 1;
610:     }
611:   }));
612: 
613:   if (formed > 0) log.info({ formed }, 'Formed and enqueued alert batches');
614:   return formed;
615: }
616: 
617: async function mapBounded<T, R>(items: T[], limit: number, fn: (item: T) => Promise<R>): Promise<PromiseSettledResult<R>[]> {
618:   const results: PromiseSettledResult<R>[] = new Array(items.length);
619:   let cursor = 0;
620:   const lane = async (): Promise<void> => {
621:     while (cursor < items.length) {
622:       const i = cursor++;
623:       const item = items[i]!;
624:       try { results[i] = { status: 'fulfilled', value: await fn(item) }; }
625:       catch (reason) { results[i] = { status: 'rejected', reason }; }
626:     }
627:   };
628:   await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(limit, items.length) }, lane));
629:   return results;
630: }

The duplicate `alert.decide` path is confirmed: it independently chooses requested channels and inserts jobs. I’m converting it into a compatibility guard that forwards only already-canonical V2 jobs, and removing its independent producer registration from the worker path so `AlertRuntimeEngines` is the sole V2 producer.

I’m inspecting the producer that enqueues `alert.decide` before removing its worker registration. The safe consolidation is to route that producer into the same canonical runtime path, not silently drop queued decisions.

177:     if (!effective.enabled || effective.conditions.length === 0) {
178:       summary.skipped += 1;
179:       return;
180:     }
181: 
182:     try {
183:       const evaluable: EvaluableCondition[] = effective.conditions.map((condition) => ({
184:         id: condition.id,
185:         conditionGroupId: condition.condition_group_id,
186:         fieldPath: condition.field_path,
187:         operator: condition.operator,
188:         thresholdValue: condition.threshold_value,
189:         isRequired: condition.is_required,
190:       }));
191:       const result = evaluateRule(payload.values, evaluable);
192:       const observed = firstObservedValue(result.conditionResults);
193:       const threshold = firstThresholdValue(effective.conditions);
194:       const scopeHash = hash([
195:         rule.organization_id,
196:         rule.id,
197:         effective.bindingId ?? '',
198:         scope.projectId ?? '',
199:         scope.environment ?? '',
200:         scope.service ?? '',
201:         scope.endpoint ?? '',
202:       ].join(':'));
203:       const states = await this.runtime.getRuleEvalStates([scopeHash]);
204:       const previous = states[0] ?? null;
205:       const now = payload.observedAt;
206:       summary.evaluated += 1;
207: 
208:       if (!result.matched) {
209:         await this.runtime.upsertRuleEvalState({
210:           scopeHash,
211:           organizationId: rule.organization_id,
212:           ruleId: rule.id,
213:           bindingId: effective.bindingId,
214:           projectId: scope.projectId ?? null,
215:           environment: scope.environment ?? null,
216:           service: scope.service ?? null,
217:           endpoint: scope.endpoint ?? null,
218:           consecutiveBreaches: 0,
219:           isBreaching: false,
220:           evaluatedAt: now,
221:           recoveredAt: previous?.is_breaching ? now : null,
222:         });
223:         if (previous?.is_breaching) {
224:           await this.appendDecision(rule, effective, scope, payload, engine, 'recovered', observed, threshold);
225:           summary.recovered += 1;
226:         }
227:         return;
228:       }
229: 
230:       const consecutive = (previous?.is_breaching ? previous.consecutive_breaches : 0) + 1;
231:       const shouldFire = consecutive >= effective.consecutiveBreaches;
232:       const coolingDown = previous?.last_fired_at
233:         ? now.getTime() - previous.last_fired_at.getTime() < effective.cooldownSeconds * 1000
234:         : false;
235: 
236:       await this.runtime.upsertRuleEvalState({
237:         scopeHash,
238:         organizationId: rule.organization_id,
239:         ruleId: rule.id,
240:         bindingId: effective.bindingId,
241:         projectId: scope.projectId ?? null,
242:         environment: scope.environment ?? null,
243:         service: scope.service ?? null,
244:         endpoint: scope.endpoint ?? null,
245:         consecutiveBreaches: consecutive,
246:         isBreaching: true,
247:         evaluatedAt: now,
248:         firedAt: shouldFire && !coolingDown ? now : null,
249:       });
250: 
251:       if (!shouldFire) {
252:         summary.suppressed += 1;
253:         return;
254:       }
255:       if (coolingDown) {
256:         summary.suppressed += 1;
257:         return;
258:       }
259: 
260:       await this.appendDecision(rule, effective, scope, payload, engine, 'fired', observed, threshold);
261:       summary.fired += 1;
262:     } catch (err) {
263:       summary.failed += 1;
264:       this.log.error({ err, ruleId: rule.id, orgId: rule.organization_id }, 'Runtime alert evaluation failed');
265:     }
266:   }

4:  * Job types:

7:  *   - alert.escalation-sweep    — advance due escalations + resume expired acks
8:  *   - alert.auto-resolve        — auto-resolve stale firing alerts
